providers.description: Atalanta is a mathematical AI company building provably correct decision-making for the world's most important missions. Its flagship platform, Argo, is described as the first software understanding platform - it uses mathematical proof and formal verification to establish safety, security, and performance guarantees for software-defined and autonomous systems at operational speed, moving beyond the limits of traditional testing. Argo identifies failure modes before deployment and verifies compliance with critical constraints across energy (nuclear and grid control systems), space (satellite and communications networks), and defense (complex military systems and data isolation). Atalanta was founded by Anjana Rajan and Jonathan Ring, is headquartered in Washington, D.C., and is backed by Felicis and In-Q-Tel.

providers.name: Canopy Aerospace & Defense
providers.description: Canopy Aerospace & Defense (Canopy A&D) is a vertically integrated advanced materials platform serving the aerospace, defense, space, maritime, and power-electronics industries. The company manufactures and delivers highly specialized materials with exceptional insulative, absorptive, and signal-reducing characteristics, including thermal protection systems (TPS), ultra-high-temperature ceramics, additive-manufactured ceramic components, multi-layer insulation and soft goods, and composite structures. Formed by Trive Capital through the combination of Canopy Aerospace, Hera Technologies, and MSM Industries, Canopy partners with OEMs from initial design and R&D through turnkey manufacturing and refurbishment of reusable platforms, operating facilities across the US, UK, and Netherlands. This is a physical materials manufacturer and publishes no public developer API; this profile captures its web and identity surface.

providers.name: Kodiak Robotics
providers.description: Kodiak Robotics, which now operates publicly as Kodiak AI, is an autonomous vehicle company founded in April 2018 by CEO Don Burnette and headquartered in California with a Texas operations center. Its flagship product is the Kodiak Driver, an AI-driven autonomy system that pairs onboard artificial intelligence with modular, swappable sensor hardware and offboard services so that a single driverless stack can be carried across different vehicle platforms. The company sells into three markets — long-haul trucking, defense, and industrial ground transportation — and positions driverless operation as a safety improvement, citing that more than 85% of U.S. truck crashes are caused by human error. Kodiak reports more than 2.6 million autonomous miles driven and over 7,000 loads delivered. Kodiak publishes no public developer API, API documentation, developer portal, or SDKs; enrichment probes of kodiak.ai found no /.well-known/ discovery documents and no api/docs/developer subdomains. It does publish an llms.txt, an RSS news feed, and a corporate safety report, so this profile is maintained as a company record rather than an API producer profile.

providers.name: World View
providers.description: World View (World View Enterprises) is a Tucson, Arizona-based stratospheric balloon company focused on remote sensing and persistent intelligence, surveillance, and reconnaissance (ISR). Its uncrewed high-altitude balloons carry EO/FMV, IR, SAR, and hyperspectral sensors for defense, government, and commercial missions. Acquired by Ondas Holdings in 2026, it now operates as part of the Ondas Sentinel multi-domain intelligence platform, with partnerships including Palantir and Sierra Nevada Corporation. World View publishes no public developer program or API.

providers.name: Airspace Intelligence
providers.description: Air Space Intelligence (ASI) builds AI software for mission-critical, geospatial operations across aviation, defense, logistics, and energy. Its Prescience platform fuses data, models operational domains, runs predictive simulations, and optimizes complex operations in real time — spanning airline operations, air traffic management, global logistics, defense (space, air, land, sea), and energy grids. ASI holds an $875M FAA contract to help modernize the U.S. National Airspace System and works with partners including Alaska Airlines, National Grid, and the U.S. Air Force. As of this profile the company publishes no public developer API, OpenAPI specification, or developer portal.

providers.name: Heven AeroTech
providers.description: Heven AeroTech (formerly Heven Drones) is a Dulles, Virginia headquartered manufacturer of hydrogen fuel-cell powered, runway-independent unmanned aircraft systems built for defense, national security and public safety missions. Founded in 2019, the company designs its own hydrogen propulsion stack and ships six named airframes — Raider, Z1, H2D55, Refueler, Atlas and Urban X — marketed on multi-hour endurance, low thermal and acoustic signature, and rapid payload and hydrogen-tank swaps. The Z1 is listed as a Blue UAS Select platform and the H2D55, Raider and Z1 are advertised as NDAA compliant. Heven operates sites in Dulles VA, Bingen WA, Mevo Carmel Israel and Mumbai India, and raised a $100M Series B led by IonQ. Heven AeroTech is a hardware manufacturer: it publishes no public developer program, API, SDK or machine-readable contract.

providers.name: Cubic Corporation
providers.description: Cubic Corporation is a major US corporation and Fortune 1000 company. The Cubic Corporation API provides programmatic access to its platform services, data, and integrations for enterprise customers and partners.

providers.name: HEICO Corporation
providers.description: HEICO Corporation is a major US corporation and Fortune 1000 company. The HEICO Corporation API provides programmatic access to its platform services, data, and integrations for enterprise customers and partners.

providers.name: Kratos Defense & Security Solutions
providers.description: Kratos Defense & Security Solutions is a major US corporation and Fortune 1000 company. The Kratos Defense & Security Solutions API provides programmatic access to its platform services, data, and integrations for enterprise customers and partners.

providers.name: Elroy Air
providers.description: Elroy Air develops autonomous vertical takeoff and landing (VTOL) cargo aircraft for defense, commercial, and rapid-response logistics. Its flagship Chaparral is a hybrid-electric aircraft designed to carry up to 300 pounds of cargo across roughly 300 miles with no crew onboard, taking off and landing vertically and cruising autonomously between points. Founded in 2016 and based in San Francisco, the company works with partners including FedEx, NASA, the U.S. Air Force, and Lockheed Martin, and was selected for the U.S. Department of Transportation eVTOL Integration Pilot Program. Elroy Air is a hardware and autonomy company; it does not currently publish a public developer API, OpenAPI, SDKs, or MCP surface. This profile was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio lead and enriched with identity and domain-security data.

providers.name: Merlin Labs
providers.description: Merlin (Merlin Labs, Inc., NASDAQ: MRLN) is a Boston-headquartered aerospace and defense company founded in 2018 that builds takeoff-to-touchdown flight autonomy for legacy and next-generation aircraft. Its product is the Merlin Pilot, an aircraft-agnostic, AI-powered autonomy stack that pairs machine-learning mission planning with deterministic, hardcoded fallback flight systems, and that has flown hundreds of autonomous flights from test facilities in Kerikeri (New Zealand), Quonset Point (Rhode Island) and Bedford/Hanscom (Massachusetts). Merlin is a prime contractor to USSOCOM for C-130J autonomy, works with the U.S. Air Force on KC-135 tanker autonomy, and collaborates with Northrop Grumman, Honeywell, GE Aerospace and Israel Aerospace Industries. The company holds a New Zealand Part 146 aircraft design organization designation and reached Stage of Involvement 3 (SOI 3) with the Civil Aviation Authority of New Zealand in August 2026. Merlin became publicly traded in March 2026 through a business combination with Inflection Point Acquisition Corp IV. Merlin sells embedded flight-autonomy software to aircraft OEMs, primes and government programs; it publishes no public developer program, API, SDK or machine-readable contract.

providers.name: Skyryse
providers.description: Skyryse is an El Segundo, California aviation technology company founded in 2016 by Mark Groden and Mitch Adler that builds SkyOS, a universal operating system for flight. SkyOS is a retrofittable hardware and software stack that replaces complex mechanical flight controls with a triply redundant, software-driven system, letting a pilot fly an airplane or helicopter with a single control stick and touchscreens. The platform delivers simplified flight controls, inherent stability, automated maneuvers, emergency autorotation, automated zero-visibility landing, envelope protection, and optionally piloted capability. Skyryse also produces Skyryse One, a SkyOS-powered production helicopter, and Skylar, a universal AI flight assistant. Customers and partners span the U.S. military, law enforcement, Cal Fire, emergency medical services, disaster response, and private operators. In February 2026 the company raised over $300 million in Series C funding at a $1.15 billion post-money valuation, co-led by Autopilot and Fidelity Investments. Skyryse operates as a certified-avionics and aircraft manufacturer and does not publish a public developer API, SDK, or developer portal.

providers.name: TurbineOne
providers.description: TurbineOne builds a frontline AI/ML platform that turns raw sensor data into real-time detection, classification, and targeting at the edge for defense and national-security missions. Its product suite spans Frontline Perception (edge computer vision on live sensor feeds), Frontline Command, Frontline Autonomy, a Model Hub for managing and deploying ML models, and EdgeWorks, a program that brings warfighters, mission teams, and engineers together to develop and validate mission capabilities for contested, disconnected environments. The company was founded on expertise in artificial intelligence, mesh networking, and sensing technology, and positions its work as "Responsible AI for our nation's heroes." It is backed by Bessemer Venture Partners. TurbineOne publishes no public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface; this profile captures its public identity, GitHub organization, and a live domain-security probe.

bands.blurb: Index entry only; little beyond a description and a link.

providers.name: Defense Advanced Research Projects Agency
providers.description: Since 1958, DARPA has held to an enduring mission: to create technological surprise for U.S. national security. Working with innovators inside and outside government, DARPA invests in transformational breakthroughs across biological technologies, defense sciences, information innovation, microsystems, strategic technology, and tactical technology. DARPA does not expose public developer APIs but does publish an RSS news feed and program information through its website.

providers.name: Hadrian
providers.description: Hadrian (Hadrian Automation) is a Los Angeles-area precision-manufacturing company founded in 2020 by Chris Power, building software-driven, AI-powered factories that produce high-tolerance machined components for the aerospace and defense industrial base — including parts for rockets, satellites, jets, drones, and missiles. The company's core software stack is Opus, described as a full-stack, AI-powered Factory Autonomy platform that interprets legacy engineering designs, automates CNC machining, inspection, tool-path optimization, adaptive programming, scheduling, and quality assurance, and enables new operators to be productive in 30 days or less. Hadrian operates multiple factories — Factory 2 (F2) and Factory X (FX) in Torrance, California, and Factory 3 (F3) in Mesa, Arizona — and offers three commercial models: precision component manufacturing, Manufacturing-as-a-Service (dedicated automation cells for a single customer), and Factories-as-a-Service (turnkey factory design and operation). Customers and partners include major aerospace and defense primes such as Lockheed Martin. Hadrian has also launched an additive manufacturing division to expand U.S. defense production capacity. The Opus platform is internal-only — Hadrian sells finished precision parts and factory capacity, not software access — and there is no public developer API, SDK, GitHub organization, or open-source release for Opus or any Hadrian system.

providers.name: Kilsar
providers.description: Kilsar is an AI-powered maintenance training and operations platform for the aviation, defense, and industrial sectors. Its flagship product, Orion, turns static technical manuals and maintenance procedures into intelligent, guided workflows so technicians learn faster and perform complex tasks correctly. The platform provides AI-assisted search across operational and maintenance manuals, dynamic data storage and library management, custom workflow and procedure building, real-time task tracking and work-log monitoring, and predictive maintenance and troubleshooting guidance. Kilsar promises measurable outcomes including reduced downtime, faster mean-time-to-repair, and increased equipment uptime. Kilsar is a Techstars-backed company. As of this profile it publishes a marketing site and a Secureframe-hosted trust center but no public API, developer documentation, or SDKs.

providers.name: BAE Systems
providers.description: BAE Systems is a British multinational defense, security, and aerospace company and one of the largest defense contractors globally. BAE Systems does not publish public developer APIs; technology integration is delivered through classified and ITAR-controlled customer programs, the Discover supplier portal, defense-program-specific data exchanges (e.g. F-35 ALIS / ODIN, Eurofighter), and FMS / government-to-government channels.

providers.name: American Superconductor Corporation
providers.description: American Superconductor Corporation (AMSC) is a Ayer, Massachusetts based power systems company that designs and deploys grid interconnection, power protection, and power supply solutions for the energy, renewables, industrial, utility, and military sectors. Its portfolio spans grid systems such as D-VAR dynamic reactive compensation and STATCOM, ship protection and degaussing systems for naval defense, wind turbine electrical control systems, and Amperium high-temperature superconductor wire. AMSC was surfaced as a portfolio company of kleiner-perkins and added to the API Evangelist network. This is a public-company / hardtech profile with no public developer API surface; the enrichment pass captured domain-security posture and corporate link properties only.

providers.name: AMSC
providers.description: American Superconductor Corporation (AMSC) is a power control systems company headquartered in Ayer, Massachusetts, and traded publicly on NASDAQ under the ticker AMSC. The company designs and delivers grid and power-electronics solutions across three specialties - power supply, power protection, and power innovation - serving the energy, renewables, utility, industrial, materials, and military sectors. Its offerings span grid capacity and resiliency systems, renewable generation integration, industrial process power control, and shipboard power protection for naval defense. AMSC is an early Battery Ventures portfolio investment. AMSC does not currently publish a public developer API, SDK, or developer portal; this profile captures the company's corporate identity and domain security posture within the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Arx Robotics
providers.description: ARX Robotics is a German defense-technology company building autonomous mobile robots and a software-defined digitalization platform for European armed forces and commercial operators. Its product line includes Gereon, a small tracked reconnaissance and casualty-evacuation robot; Hector, a larger autonomous all-terrain ground vehicle for scalable land operations; and Mithra OS, a digitalization platform that modernizes legacy vehicle fleets through software integration. ARX positions itself around strengthening Europe's technological resilience and sovereignty with mission-ready, software-defined unmanned ground systems. The company was surfaced as a portfolio company of Speedinvest and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment; it publishes no public developer, API, or documentation surface at this time.

providers.name: Blue Water Autonomy
providers.description: Blue Water Autonomy is a Boston-based defense technology company building autonomous warships for open-ocean operations, with the goal of revitalizing U.S. shipbuilding through scalable, reliable, uncrewed naval vessels. Founded in 2025 by Rylan Hamilton (ex-U.S. Navy officer and founder of 6 River Systems), Scott N. Miller (ocean engineer and early iRobot engineer), and Austin Gray (former Navy intelligence officer), the company unveiled its 190-foot Liberty Class autonomous ship platform for the U.S. Navy in February 2026. Backed by a $50M Series A led by GV, Blue Water Autonomy operates from offices in Boston MA, Washington DC, Morgan City LA, and San Diego CA. This is a company profile in the API Evangelist network; the company publishes no public API, developer portal, or SDK surface as of this enrichment pass.

providers.name: Bluewhite (fka Blue White Robotics)
providers.description: Bluewhite (formerly Blue White Robotics) is an autonomy company that builds an AI-powered "Field Intelligence" physical-AI engine for operating vehicles in demanding, unstructured, real-world environments. Founded in Israel, the company first commercialized autonomous agriculture — retrofitting existing tractor fleets with an aftermarket autonomy kit for driverless spraying, mowing, and other field operations — and has since extended the same edge-processing autonomy stack to defense and security missions through OEM integrations and complete unmanned ground vehicles (UGVs). Bluewhite is a portfolio company of Insight Partners. The company exposes no public developer API, developer portal, or technical documentation; this API Evangelist profile tracks its identity and public web surface.

providers.name: Dedrone
providers.description: Dedrone is a counter-drone (counter-UAS) airspace security company that detects, tracks, identifies, and helps mitigate unauthorized drones and unmanned aerial systems. Its AI-powered sensor platform combines RF detection, radar, cameras, and mitigation technologies to protect airports, critical infrastructure, correctional facilities, stadiums, and government and military sites. Dedrone was acquired by Axon and operates as its counter-drone / airspace-security line. Surfaced through the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of Felicis and Menlo Ventures; no public developer API, portal, or specification was found during enrichment.

providers.name: Forterra
providers.description: Forterra is a defense autonomy company headquartered in Clarksburg, Maryland, that builds combat-proven autonomous mission systems for ground operations in contested, GPS-denied, off-road environments. Founded in 2002 as Robotic Research and rebranded as Forterra, it retrofits existing military and commercial vehicles with self-driving capability through its AutoDrive autonomous driving system, the TerraLink modular vehicle-management and command-and-control platform, and the OASIS open architecture that lets the government and third-party developers add sensors, effectors, and payloads without vendor lock-in. Additional offerings span resilient communications, sensing, and ruggedized edge-compute hardware. The company is backed by SoftBank Vision Fund 2 and Enlightenment Capital and supplies autonomy to multiple active U.S. Department of Defense programs. Forterra does not publish a public developer API, SDKs, or self-service developer portal; its systems are delivered as government and defense-integration programs.

providers.name: Mesodyne
providers.description: Mesodyne is an MIT-founded engineering and manufacturing company (established 2018) that builds the LightCell, a patented thermophotovoltaic power generator which converts liquid and gaseous fuels — gasoline, diesel, propane, jet fuel, and hydrogen — directly into silent electricity with more than ten times the energy density of batteries. Designed for military, tactical, drone, and off-grid use, it operates day or night across extreme environments with low heat and emissions signatures and no routine maintenance. Mesodyne publishes no public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface; this profile captures the company identity and its domain-security posture.

providers.name: Reach
providers.description: Reach Power (Reach Labs) is a Y Combinator-backed (S2015) wireless power company building long-range wireless energy distribution networks, aiming to "do for power what Wi-Fi did for data." Its patented, AI-driven power-beaming systems use adaptive metamaterial antennas to steer electromagnetic waves and deliver electricity through the air to multiple devices simultaneously, scaling from microwatts to kilowatts across both mobile and stationary transmitters. Reach serves defense and intelligence, manufacturing and logistics, and public safety markets, powering autonomous vehicles, industrial robotics, sensors, and drones. Partners and customers include the U.S. Department of Defense, NASA, DARPA, the U.S. Army and Air Force, Aisin/Toyota, and Panasonic. The company is headquartered in San Francisco. As of this profile, Reach publishes no public developer API, SDK, or developer portal; this is a hardware and energy-infrastructure company rather than an API platform.

providers.name: Toka
providers.description: Toka is a defense and intelligence technology company, founded in 2017-2018 and headquartered in Maryland with R&D in Israel, that develops signals intelligence, ISR, cyber operations, and force protection capabilities exclusively for militaries, homeland security organizations, intelligence agencies, and law enforcement in the United States and allied nations. Backed by Andreessen Horowitz (a16z), Eclipse Ventures, and Dell Technologies Capital, Toka sells government-facing capability platforms and cyber capacity-building services rather than a public developer or API surface, and publishes no developer portal, documentation, or machine-readable API artifacts.

providers.name: Vita Inclinata
providers.description: Vita Inclinata Technologies is a Colorado-based hardware company that builds physics-based load stabilization systems for helicopter hoists and construction cranes, eliminating the dangerous spin and sway of suspended loads. Its ecosystem spans Vita Aerospace (helicopter and rescue hoist stabilization), Vita Industrial (crane and construction load control), Air Rescue Systems (hoist training and products), and the Vita Rescue System used in military MEDEVAC operations. The company is Techstars-backed. It was surfaced as a portfolio-company lead and added to the API Evangelist network; as a physical-hardware manufacturer it currently publishes no public developer API, SDK, or technical integration surface.

providers.name: ZeroAvia
providers.description: ZeroAvia is a UK/US hydrogen-electric aviation company founded in 2017 by Valery Miftakhov, developing hydrogen fuel cell and electric propulsion systems for commercial aircraft. Its powertrain line runs from the ZA600 (600kW, 10-20 seat regional turboprops) through the ZA2000 (2-5MW, 40-80 seat turboprops) to the ZA2000 RJ (5MW+, up to 90 seat regional jets), alongside a component business selling electric propulsion systems, inverters, electric motors and HTPEM/SuperStack fuel cell stacks to other clean-aviation manufacturers, plus a hydrogen airport refuelling ecosystem of electrolyzers, mobile refuelers and LH2 development. It operates from Cotswold Airport in Kemble, UK and from Everett, Washington, and holds FAA and CAA experimental certificates for its flight-test aircraft. ZeroAvia sells certified aerospace hardware to airframers, airlines, lessors and defense customers; it publishes no public developer API, SDK or developer portal.

providers.name: Divergent
providers.description: Divergent Technologies, Inc. is a Torrance and Long Beach, California manufacturer that built the Divergent Adaptive Production System (DAPS), an end-to-end software-hardware production system for industrial digital manufacturing. DAPS pairs AI-driven generative design software with in-house metal additive manufacturing — the Monolith One printer, compatible with aluminum, nickel, steel and titanium alloys — and automated fixtureless robotic assembly, so complex multi-part structures can be engineered, printed and assembled without fixed tooling. Founded in 2013 by Kevin and Lukas Czinger, the company is a Tier 1 supplier to global automotive OEMs and has expanded into aerospace and defense, including selection under the US Air Force Eglin Wide Agile Acquisition Contract. Divergent sells manufactured structures and production capacity, not software: it publishes no developer portal, no public API, and no machine-readable contract of any kind.

providers.name: BETA Technologies
providers.description: BETA Technologies is a Vermont-based aerospace company that designs and manufactures all-electric aircraft and the supporting electric aviation charging network. BETA produces two variants of its ALIA platform: ALIA CTOL (conventional take-off and landing) and ALIA VTOL (vertical take-off and landing), each carrying a pilot plus five passengers or equivalent cargo, with demonstrated range of 336 nautical miles and sub-hour recharge. BETA's Charge Cube is an interoperable multimodal charger now deployed at sites across the U.S. covering more than 50 million people within 50 miles, and the company operates a 188,000-square-foot net-zero manufacturing facility in South Burlington, Vermont. Customers include UPS, United Therapeutics, the U.S. Air Force and U.S. Army (via AFWERX Agility Prime), Air New Zealand, Bristow, Surf Air Mobility, and other early operators; BETA was selected for seven of the eight FAA eVTOL Integration Pilot Program initiatives.

providers.name: Niron Magnetics
providers.description: Niron Magnetics is a U.S. advanced-manufacturing company commercializing high-performance permanent magnets made from Iron Nitride rather than rare-earth elements. Spun out of University of Minnesota and U.S. Department of Energy ARPA-E research and founded in 2013, the company holds 150+ patents around its Clean Earth Magnet technology and is building the first full-scale Iron Nitride magnet plant in Sartell, Minnesota, alongside its Minneapolis headquarters and a Washington, D.C. policy office. Its magnets target electric-motor, automotive, consumer-audio, industrial and defense applications, with announced collaborations including Stellantis, Moog, Aspina, FaitalPRO, MATTER and Bimotal. Niron Magnetics is a materials and hardware manufacturer: it publishes no developer program, no public API, and no machine-readable API contract.

providers.name: Reliable Robotics
providers.description: Reliable Robotics is a California-based aerospace company developing continuous autopilot and remote piloting systems that retrofit existing fixed-wing aircraft for automated and remotely supervised flight across all phases (taxi, take-off, cruise, landing). The company has flown automated Cessna 208 Caravan demonstrations including a fully uncrewed take-off and landing in 2023, and is pursuing FAA Part 23 supplemental type certification for its automation system. Reliable Robotics has contracts with the U.S. Air Force AFWERX program and the Defense Innovation Unit to evaluate automated cargo and ISR missions on platforms including the Cessna 208, and has partnered with Textron Aviation on certification work. The company's founders are alumni of SpaceX and Tesla autopilot teams. Reliable Robotics is partner- and government-gated and does not currently offer public consumer or developer APIs.

providers.name: Seurat Technologies
providers.description: Seurat Technologies is a Wilmington, Massachusetts contract manufacturer that produces high-volume metal parts using its proprietary Area Printing technology, a Laser Powderbed Fusion (LPBF) additive process that decouples print speed from resolution and is positioned as roughly 10x more productive than conventional LPBF. Seurat does not sell 3D printers; it sells parts, qualifying customer designs through its Area Printing Production (APP) qualification program and then mass-producing them at localized factories for consumer electronics, automotive, energy, aerospace and defense OEMs. The company markets its process on reshoring, supply-chain resilience, tariff resistance and decarbonization, and engages customers through a quote / upload-your-part motion rather than any developer-facing product.

providers.name: Sierra Space
providers.description: Sierra Space is a commercial space and defense technology company headquartered in Louisville, Colorado, spun out of Sierra Nevada Corporation as an independent entity in April 2021 and building on more than three decades of spaceflight heritage. The company designs and manufactures the Dream Chaser reusable lifting-body spaceplane and Shooting Star cargo module, the LIFE expandable space habitat and the Orbital Reef commercial space station developed with Blue Origin, Eclipse-class satellites for national security and on-orbit servicing missions, VORTEX rocket propulsion and hypersonics, space solar arrays and electrical power systems, environmental control and life support systems, and a broad spaceflight hardware catalog spanning valves, regulators, radiators, sensors, actuators, docking and berthing systems, deployable structures and launch adapters. Sierra Space states it has delivered more than 4,000 space systems, subsystems and components across more than 500 space missions. It is a hardware and mission-systems manufacturer rather than a software platform: as of this profiling pass it publishes no public developer portal, API documentation or machine-readable API contract.

providers.name: Vake
providers.description: VAKE is a Norwegian maritime domain awareness company that detects, identifies, and tracks "dark vessels" from space. The VAKE platform fuses satellite imagery, AIS signals, and machine learning to reveal hidden vessel activity at sea for governments and industry. Its three products are Pathfinder, which reconstructs a vessel's past, present, and predicted movements and searches satellite imagery for vessels that go AIS-dark; Overwatch, which monitors an Area of Interest around ports, critical infrastructure, and economic zones to surface unreported activity such as illegal fishing, transshipments, and spoofing; and Clearview, a machine-learning service that identifies dark-vessel observations in multispectral satellite imagery against a global vessel-signature database spanning 2016 to today. The platform is delivered as a web application (studio.vake.ai) backed by a private API (api.nemme.io); onboarding is sales-led rather than self-serve.

providers.name: Ducommun
providers.description: Ducommun is a major US corporation and Fortune 1000 company. The Ducommun API provides programmatic access to its platform services, data, and integrations for enterprise customers and partners.

providers.name: Freeform
providers.description: Freeform is an AI-native advanced manufacturing company founded by former SpaceX engineers, building a network of autonomous factories that sense, learn, predict, and control metal formation for high-performance metal additive manufacturing (metal 3D printing). Freeform integrates hardware, sensors, controls, and software to move parts from prototype to full-scale production for aerospace, defense, aviation, advanced energy, consumer electronics, and automotive customers. It is a physical-AI / advanced-manufacturing business rather than a software API platform, so as of this profile it exposes no public developer API, SDKs, or developer documentation.

providers.name: Insitu
providers.description: Insitu Inc. is a wholly owned subsidiary of The Boeing Company that designs, builds, and operates uncrewed aerial systems (UAS) and related intelligence, surveillance, and reconnaissance technologies for defense and government customers. Its product line includes the Integrator, ScanEagle, and RQ-21A air vehicles alongside imaging payloads, ground control stations, and mission software such as TacitView, the Media Management Suite, and the Tungsten SDK. Insitu delivers end-to-end capabilities for collecting, processing, and distributing information, with more than 1.6 million operational flight hours across 30-plus international customers. Insitu operates as a defense contractor and publishes no public developer API, developer portal, or OpenAPI surface.

providers.name: Ocean Aero
providers.description: Ocean Aero is a Gulfport, Mississippi maritime robotics manufacturer that designs, builds and operates the Triton, an environmentally powered Autonomous Underwater and Surface Vehicle (AUSV) that can both sail on the surface and submerge to collect data above and below the waterline and relay it back to shore. The 14-foot platform harvests wind and solar energy, carries pre-packaged or custom payloads for defense, ocean research and offshore energy missions, and is managed through Ocean Aero's own proprietary mission-control GUI with fleet-wide waypoint and payload management. As of this profile Ocean Aero sells vehicles, payloads and mission services — it publishes no public developer program, no API reference and no machine-readable API contract.

providers.name: Red 6
providers.description: Red 6 (Red Six Aerospace, Inc.) is a defense technology company founded in 2018 that builds outdoor, high-speed augmented reality for military aviation training. Its flagship product, ATARS (Advanced Tactical Augmented Reality System), pairs the EVE (Enhanced Visual Environment) helmet-mounted display — 160-degree field of view, 18,000 nits, 10ms latency, full color — with an AI-driven multiplayer network so real pilots in real aircraft can fly and maneuver against synthetically generated adversaries in real time, in daylight. A companion system, ARCADE (Augmented Reality Command and Analytic Data Environment), handles mission planning, briefing and three-dimensional debrief. ATARS has been integrated or trialed on the USAF F-16 and MC-130, the RAF Hawk T-2, Boeing's AH-64E Apache CATT, and the Lockheed Martin / Korea Aerospace Industries T-50/TF-50. Red 6 is ISO 9001:2015 and AS9100D certified. It publishes no public developer program, API, SDK or machine-readable contract — its software surface is delivered through defense programs and OEM integrations rather than a self-serve developer platform.

providers.name: Sales Patriot
providers.description: SalesPatriot deploys artificial intelligence into enterprise supply chain operations, embedding engineers onsite to build custom AI solutions that integrate fragmented business systems (ERP, CRM, email, spreadsheets, and supplier portals) and automate routine workflows. The platform aggregates data from scattered sources into a unified, searchable system, automates tasks such as quoting, sourcing, and data entry, and visualizes real-time operational metrics for executives. It serves defense contracting and procurement, complex multi-source procurement operations, and high-volume distribution. SalesPatriot is a portfolio company of CRV. This profile was added to the API Evangelist network and enriched by the pipeline; the company publishes no public developer or API surface at this time.

providers.name: Senra Systems
providers.description: Senra Systems is an aerospace wire harness manufacturer based in Redondo Beach, California, that unites design, data, and production under one roof. The company builds complex electrical wire harnesses for aerospace and defense programs, spanning wire harness design and engineering support, prototype through full-rate production, component selection and supply chain optimization, and precision automation in a 15,000 square foot smart-manufacturing facility. Senra positions itself as delivering harnesses at roughly four times the speed of traditional vendors while maintaining aerospace-grade quality and certifications. Senra Systems is backed by Sequoia Capital, Andreessen Horowitz, Founders Fund, 8VC, and General Catalyst. The company does not currently publish a public API, developer portal, or SDKs.

providers.name: AAR Corp
providers.description: AAR Corp is a global aerospace and defense aftermarket solutions company and the number one aviation maintenance, repair, and overhaul (MRO) provider in North America. They offer aircraft parts supply, airframe and component MRO, integrated software solutions (Trax, Aerostrat, Airinmar), and expeditionary services to commercial airlines and government customers worldwide.

providers.name: Parsons Corporation
providers.description: Parsons Corporation is a major US corporation and Fortune 1000 company. The Parsons Corporation API provides programmatic access to its platform services, data, and integrations for enterprise customers and partners.

providers.name: Westmag
providers.description: Western Magnetics (Westmag) designs and manufactures brushless DC (BLDC) drone motors and robot actuators in South San Francisco, California. Built and scaled in America and NDAA-compliant from day one, Westmag is a vertically integrated motor company spanning design, manufacturing, and supply chain — producing high-volume BLDC drone motors for Group 1, 2, and 3 UAS platforms (20-100mm stators, Kv 100-3,000, outrunner and inrunner) and integrated actuators for humanoid and mobile robots (torque 1-150Nm, 24-48V, gearing 6:1-12:1). Founded by David Hansen (CEO) and Jordan Sanders (COO) and backed by Andreessen Horowitz, Founders Fund, Lux Capital, Menlo Ventures, and NFDG. This is a hardware company; it currently exposes no public developer API surface.

providers.name: ABL Space Systems
providers.description: ABL Space Systems is an American launch vehicle company founded in 2017 by Harry O'Hanley and Dan Piemont, headquartered in El Segundo, California, with operations at the Port of Long Beach, Mojave and Kodiak, Alaska. ABL built RS1, a two-stage, kerosene/liquid-oxygen small satellite launch vehicle designed to deliver 1,350 kg to low Earth orbit and 1,000 kg to sun-synchronous orbit, powered by nine in-house additively manufactured E2 engines on the first stage and one on the second. Its companion GS0 ground system packages an entire orbital launch site into standard shipping containers so a pad can be activated anywhere with a flat concrete surface and moved by land, sea or air. RS1 attempted its first orbital flight from Pacific Spaceport Complex Kodiak in January 2023 and was lost shortly after liftoff; a second vehicle was destroyed during preflight static-fire testing in July 2024. In November 2024 the company announced its exit from the commercial orbital launch market, and in February 2025 it rebranded as Long Wall, refocusing on containerized missile defense — the Cyclops exoatmospheric interceptor, RSX low-cost liquid boosters for flight testing and threat replication, and the Ironwood ground support equipment line. ABL/Long Wall is an aerospace and defense hardware manufacturer: it publishes no public developer API, SDK, machine-readable API contract or developer portal.

providers.name: Castelion
providers.description: Castelion is a vertically integrated defense technology company that designs, tests, and manufactures next-generation military systems, with a focus on affordable, mass-producible hypersonic strike weapons such as its Blackbeard system, built rapidly and at scale to deter future conflict. Founded by former SpaceX and defense-industry engineers, it operates manufacturing and test facilities in Torrance, CA; Rio Rancho, NM; Midland, TX; and Allen, TX. Castelion is privately held and backed by Andreessen Horowitz (a16z), General Catalyst, and Lightspeed Venture Partners. It publishes no public API, developer portal, or technical documentation; this API Evangelist profile tracks it as a company in the network.

providers.name: HavocAI
providers.description: HavocAI (Havoc) is a Providence, Rhode Island-based defense technology company building all-domain collaborative autonomy software and autonomous surface vessels for the U.S. Navy, U.S. Army and allied militaries. Its software suite pairs Havoc OS, an edge autonomy operating system for heterogeneous platforms, with Havoc C2 for one-to-many operator control, Havoc Insights for real-time sensor and telemetry analytics, and Havoc Connect, a resilient peer-to-peer overlay network for degraded or GPS-denied environments. The company builds the Rampage, Seahound, Kiakoa and Atlas autonomous surface vessels and is partnered with Hanwha on 200-foot ASVs. Enrichment probing in July 2026 found no public developer API, OpenAPI or other machine-readable contract, no developer portal or documentation, no published SDKs or packages, no MCP server, and no A2A agent card - the platform is delivered under defense contract rather than as a self-serve developer product.

providers.name: VulcanForms
providers.description: VulcanForms operates integrated digital metal manufacturing factories in the United States, combining in-house designed industrial-scale laser powder bed fusion (LPBF) additive machines, precision machining, automation, inspection, and proprietary AI-enabled software into a single end-to-end production workflow. The company produces mission-critical metal components at production scale for the aerospace, defense, medical, compute, consumer, and industrial sectors, compressing the supply chain into one secure, vertically integrated system. Headquartered in Devens, Massachusetts, VulcanForms is backed by Eclipse, 1789 Capital, D1 Capital and others. This profile currently exposes no public developer API surface.

providers.name: Whisper Aero
providers.description: Whisper Aero is a Crossville, Tennessee based aerospace company developing ultra-quiet electric ducted-fan propulsion that converts electricity into thrust with roughly 20 percent more efficiency and 20 dB less noise than conventional systems, scaling from 5 to 500 pounds of thrust and 40 to 400 knots for aviation, defense, and commercial applications. Backed by Kindred Ventures, Lux Capital, and Menlo Ventures. The company is a hardware manufacturer and, as of this enrichment pass, publishes no public developer API, portal, or documentation surface.

providers.name: Achates Power
providers.description: Achates Power is a San Diego, California engine technology company founded in 2004 by Dr. James Lemke and John Walton that develops opposed-piston, two-stroke compression-ignition engine architecture and licenses the resulting engine designs, development tools, simulation software and patents to engine manufacturers and OEMs. Its engines target passenger vehicles, medium and heavy-duty commercial trucks, military vehicles, and off-road and power-generation applications, and the company has claimed fuel-efficiency improvements of as much as 30 percent over conventional engines at comparable or better emissions. Achates Power has received U.S. Army TARDEC, Department of Energy and ARPA-E funding and partners with engine manufacturers such as Fairbanks Morse. It is a privately held hardware and engineering licensing business and publishes no public developer program, API, or machine-readable API artifacts.

providers.name: Air Company
providers.description: Air Company (AIRCO) is a carbon conversion technology company founded in 2017 by Gregory Constantine and Dr. Stafford Sheehan. Its patented Carbon Conversion Reactor mimics photosynthesis, combining captured CO2, water and green hydrogen with renewable energy to produce carbon-negative alcohols and fully formulated synthetic fuels. The company licenses its catalytic process technologies and designs deployable production systems, from the container-scale AIRCO MAD Fuel System to the AIRCO SAF Factory. Product lines are branded AIRMADE and span sustainable aviation fuel (SAF), ethanol, methanol, diesel and rocket fuel, with earlier consumer validation products including AIR Vodka and AIR Eau de Parfum. Partners and customers include the U.S. Department of Defense, U.S. Air Force, Department of Energy and NASA, alongside aviation partners such as Virgin, Air France-KLM, JetBlue and Air Canada; strategic investors include Alaska Airlines, Carbon Direct, In-Q-Tel and Toyota Ventures. Air Company publishes no public API, developer portal or machine-readable API contract as of the 2026-07-31 enrichment pass.

providers.name: Laelaps AI
providers.description: Laelaps AI is a Zurich- and UK-based autonomous security company building what it calls "the brain behind security" — a hardware-agnostic, fail-safe autonomy layer that unifies aerial, ground, and stationary robots together with a site's existing fixed cameras into a single coordinated monitoring force. The platform pairs field foundational models and visual intelligence with multi-agent coordination so that critical infrastructure and commercial and defense sites can be watched continuously, incidents detected and triaged automatically, and robots dispatched to observe and deter without a human operator watching every screen. Founded by Dr. Sophia Belser (CEO), Dr. Maria "Mania" Stamatopoulou (CRO), and Rokas Bendikas (CTO), the company is backed by Speedinvest, Expeditions Fund, Florent Venture Partners, Fund F, ESA BIC Switzerland, and NVIDIA Inception. As of this profile Laelaps AI publishes a three-page corporate website and no public developer surface — no documentation, API reference, SDKs, or machine-readable API artifacts were found.

providers.name: Science Applications International Corporation (SAIC)
providers.description: Science Applications International Corporation (SAIC) is a leading American technology integrator providing full life cycle services and solutions in the technical, engineering, and enterprise information technology markets. Headquartered in Reston, Virginia, SAIC serves the U.S. federal government with approximately $7.4 billion in annual revenues. The company delivers IT modernization, cloud computing, digital transformation, cybersecurity, AI/ML, and data analytics solutions primarily for defense, intelligence, and civilian government customers. SAIC's open source presence is at github.com/saic-oss with DevSecOps tools including Anvil (CI/CD container) and terraform modules for Kubernetes sandboxes.

providers.name: Textron
providers.description: Textron Inc. is a $14.8 billion Fortune 500 multi-industry company employing 34,000 people worldwide. Textron operates through five business segments: Bell (military and commercial helicopters), Textron Aviation (Cessna, Beechcraft, Hawker aircraft), Industrial (Kautex fuel systems, Textron Specialized Vehicles including E-Z-GO and Jacobsen), Textron Systems (defense and autonomous systems), and Textron Financial. As of 2026, Textron does not offer publicly documented developer APIs or integration portals.

providers.name: REGENT Craft
providers.description: REGENT Craft Inc. is a Rhode Island maritime mobility manufacturer building the Seaglider, an all-electric wing-in-ground-effect (WIG) vessel that floats on its hull, hydrofoils, and then flies within a wingspan of the water's surface at up to 180 mph. The company builds the 12-passenger Viceroy, the larger Monarch, and the uncrewed Squire defense drone, and operates a defense product line for ISR, contested logistics and MEDEVAC missions. REGENT is a vehicle manufacturer rather than a software company: it publishes no developer program, no public API and no machine-readable API contract. It does serve a real, hand-authored llms.txt at its website root, which is the only machine-readable artifact on its public surface.

providers.name: SATIM
providers.description: SATIM provides AI-powered analysis of Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) imagery for intelligence, surveillance, and reconnaissance (ISR) operations. Its OREC analytics engine performs automated object detection and classification on satellite and airborne SAR data (accuracy up to 95%), deployable in cloud, edge, or air-gapped environments and integrable into C2 and C4ISR workflows. OREC-Intelligence adds persistent monitoring with real-time area-of-interest change alerts and activity pattern analysis. Headquartered in Krakow, Poland, with offices in Dover, Delaware and London. Surfaced as a Techstars portfolio company; no public API surface, developer portal, SDKs, or documentation are published at this time.

providers.name: Scout
providers.description: Scout (Scout Space) is a Techstars- and venture-backed space technology company founded in 2019 that builds next-generation orbital sensing and autonomy for Space Domain Awareness (SDA). Its in-space products, first launched in 2021, let spacecraft see and understand objects around them through electro-optical and infrared sensors (the Owl long-range SDA sensor line), edge processing hardware, mission autonomy software developed with the U.S. Space Force, and mission-design analysis. Scout supplies cross-orbit intelligence and dynamic space operations to government and commercial operators and has been awarded multiple AFWERX SBIR and USSF TACFI contracts. Scout does not publish a public developer API, SDK, or developer portal; this profile captures its identity and domain-security posture for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Prewitt Ridge
providers.description: Prewitt Ridge builds SysGit, "the collaboration layer for complex hardware" — an enterprise platform that applies software development practices to systems engineering. SysGit provides Git-based version control for requirements and system models, Model-Based Systems Engineering (MBSE) workflows, AI-assisted systems engineering automation, and SysMLv2 compliance for open-standards adherence. The platform targets defense and aerospace teams, with customers including the US Air Force, GTRI, Leidos, and Anduril. Prewitt Ridge is a Techstars-backed company added to the API Evangelist network. As of this enrichment pass the company publishes no public API, SDK, developer documentation, or .well-known documents.

providers.name: USA Rare Earth
providers.description: USA Rare Earth, Inc. (Nasdaq: USAR) is an American critical-minerals and advanced-materials company building a domestic mine-to-magnet rare earth supply chain. It operates a 310,000 sq. ft. sintered neodymium-iron-boron (NdFeB) permanent magnet manufacturing facility in Stillwater, Oklahoma, and holds the Round Top heavy rare earth and critical minerals deposit in Hudspeth County, West Texas. The company produces rare earth elements, oxides, metals and sintered permanent magnets for defense, automotive, robotics, industrial and clean-energy customers, with the stated aim of reducing U.S. dependence on offshore rare earth processing and magnet production. It is a materials producer and manufacturer, not a software or data company, and publishes no public developer program, API, or machine-readable interface.

providers.name: Astranis
providers.description: Astranis designs, manufactures, and operates small, dedicated geostationary communications satellites known as MicroGEO. Each spacecraft uses radiation-hardened digital payload technology to deliver dedicated broadband capacity to specific countries, telecom operators, enterprise users, and the U.S. government. Astranis is a satellite operator and manufacturer rather than an API provider; it does not publish a public developer API.

providers.name: Code Metal
providers.description: Code Metal is a Boston-based AI company building a verifiable code translation and optimization platform for mission-critical, edge, and regulated industries including defense, automotive, semiconductor, robotics, and aerospace. The platform ingests high-level research and prototype code (Python, MATLAB, Julia) and produces optimized, edge-ready low-level code across C/C++, Rust, VHDL, Verilog, CUDA, HIP, and ONNX, using a divide-and-conquer pipeline that instruments and tests, translates and verifies functional equivalence, then optimizes and benchmarks against target CPU/GPU/FPGA runtimes. Code Metal was surfaced as a portfolio company of Accel and added to the API Evangelist network. As of this enrichment pass the company publishes no public API, developer documentation, or specification surface; this profile carries verified company identity plus a probed domain-security posture.

providers.name: GrayMatter Robotics
providers.description: GrayMatter Robotics is an American industrial AI and robotics company founded in 2020 by SK Gupta, Ariyan Kabir and Brual Shah, headquartered at a 100,000-square-foot AI Robotics Innovation Center in Carson, California. The company builds smart robotic cells for surface treatment and finishing in high-mix, high-variability manufacturing — sanding, grinding, polishing, buffing, blasting, spraying, trimming and AI-based dimensional inspection and defect detection — pairing off-the-shelf industrial robot arms, 3D scanners and tools with its own physics-informed AI stack (GMR-AI, marketed as Factory SuperIntelligence / FSI). Its flagship Scan&Sand cell 3D-scans each incoming part and generates the toolpath autonomously, so a cell can change over between parts in minutes without fixturing or teach-pendant programming, and the company claims 4-12x throughput over manual finishing with 30-70% less consumable waste. GrayMatter sells robots-as-a-service on a monthly subscription that bundles hardware, software, training, remote monitoring and 24/7 support instead of an upfront capital purchase, and counts Boeing, Caterpillar and Oshkosh among its customers. It raised a $45M Series B in June 2024 led by Wellington Management with NGP Capital, Euclidean Capital, B Capital, 3M Ventures, Calibrate VC, OCA Ventures, Pathbreaker VC, Stage Venture Partners and Swift VC participating. GrayMatter Robotics is a robotics hardware and AI systems manufacturer: as of the August 2026 enrichment pass it publishes no public developer API, developer portal, SDK, CLI or machine-readable API contract (OpenAPI, AsyncAPI, GraphQL, gRPC), no MCP server and no A2A agent card. Note that this company is unrelated to greymatter.io, the service-mesh vendor with a similar name.

providers.name: Lumotive
providers.description: Lumotive is a Seattle-based semiconductor company building programmable optics on its patented Light Control Metasurface (LCM) technology — solid-state, software-defined beam steering implemented in a standard CMOS process with no moving parts. Its products include the LM10 and LX10 LCM beam-steering chips, the LCM Evaluation Kit (LEK), the M30 iToF and NM120 3D-sensing development kits, and the M30/TX10 reference designs, applied to industrial automation, intelligent traffic systems, automotive ADAS and autonomy, defense, and optical circuit switching for AI data centers. Lumotive publishes an "Open Lidar API" — a real-time control interface for software-defined Lidar 2.0 hardware covering region-of-interest scanning, frame rate, resolution and range, plus a common point-cloud format — and ships C/C++ LCM control libraries with Python bindings alongside its evaluation kits. That interface is an embedded hardware-control API, not a public web API: no developer portal, documentation site, machine-readable specification, or self-service sign-up is published, and access is granted to selected partners through the Technology Access Program by contacting the company.

providers.name: Aerospacelab
providers.description: Aerospacelab is a vertically integrated satellite manufacturer headquartered in Mont-Saint-Guibert, Belgium, founded in 2018 by Benoit Deper. The company designs, builds, tests and operates small-to-medium satellites — its Versatile Satellite Platform (VSP-50, VSP-150, VSP-300) family plus mission-specific payloads spanning very-high-resolution and multispectral/hyperspectral Earth observation, synthetic aperture radar, radio-frequency sensing, and narrowband/broadband telecommunications — for commercial, institutional and government customers, with an explicitly ITAR-free European supply chain. It is roughly 90% vertically integrated across platforms, payloads, avionics and subsystems, has flown eight satellites in under three years, acquired Belgian space-optics firm AMOS, and is building a European satellite megafactory targeting 500 satellites per year. Aerospacelab publishes no public developer program, API documentation or machine-readable API contract; its programmatic surfaces (mission control, tasking, image-processing pipeline and data platform built under the ESA InCubed MultiSpectral Companion Mission) are delivered to contracted mission customers rather than to self-serve developers.

providers.name: Hexcel
providers.description: Hexcel Corporation (NYSE: HXL) is a global leader in advanced composite materials for the aerospace, defense and space, and industrial markets. Headquartered in Stamford, Connecticut and operating roughly 18 manufacturing facilities worldwide with about 5,800 employees, Hexcel produces HexTow carbon fiber, HexPly prepregs, HexWeb honeycomb, HexForce reinforcements, HexBond adhesives, HexFlow infusion resins, and HexTool tooling materials supplied into commercial aircraft, military platforms, space launch vehicles, wind energy blades, and industrial structures. Hexcel is a critical materials supplier to Boeing and Airbus and supports more than 100 defense programs; it has no public developer portal, REST APIs, SDKs, or machine-readable product catalog. Customer interaction with technical resources is PDF-based (datasheets, technology manuals, brochures), and the company's GitHub organization (github.com/Hexcel) is registered but empty.

providers.name: Vannevar Labs
providers.description: Vannevar Labs is a defense technology company that builds agentic AI for national security missions. Its Agent Orchestration platform fuses defense-grade foundational data, mission requirements, and strategic reasoning into mission-focused AI agents — spanning course-of-action, force-protection, information-operations, and cross-border pattern-analysis agents — used from tactical kill-chain decisions to theater-level campaigns. The company collects hard-to-reach data from adversarial information environments to train models for national security, and works across mission areas including Indo-Pacific deterrence, homeland security, and intelligent statecraft. Backed by General Catalyst; no public developer portal or API surface is published.

providers.name: Allen Control Systems
providers.description: Allen Control Systems is a defense technology company building autonomous precision weapon stations that detect, track, and neutralize unmanned aerial systems (drones) for military and partner forces. Its Bullfrog family of robotic gun mounts (M240C, M2, M230, M134) pairs passive machine-vision drone detection with autonomous fire-control targeting, synthetic training-data generation, and low-collateral engagement options such as laser dazzlers and composite rounds. The systems use an open architecture to integrate with command-and-control platforms. Backed by Craft Ventures, the company is tracked in the API Evangelist network as a defense-sector provider; it publishes no public developer API, portal, or specification at this time.

providers.name: Arondite
providers.description: Arondite is a defence technology company building Cobalt, a defence software platform for accelerated decision making that orchestrates missions and manages operational intelligence. Cobalt brings together sighting reports, real-time notifications and alerts, mapping and visualisation, task management and kanban workflows, and observation and monitoring tools to support complex military and defence operations across use cases including Hybrid Navy, C-UAS, Recce-Strike, and Site Security. Arondite combines operational and technical expertise to deliver technology with immediate, real-world impact on a global scale. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of Index Ventures. Arondite does not currently publish a public API, developer portal, SDK, or documentation surface, so this profile captures its identity and probed domain-security posture rather than API artifacts.

providers.name: Cx2
providers.description: CX2 is a defense technology company building AI-enabled electromagnetic spectrum (electronic warfare) systems for the tactical edge. Founded in 2024 and headquartered in El Segundo, California, CX2 develops attritable, machine-learning-powered hardware and software that detect, disrupt, and geolocate RF threats across land, air, sea, and space. Its flagship products are Wraith, a roughly 32-pound autonomous airborne EW platform that geolocates and identifies hostile emitters such as jammers and radars in GPS-denied environments, and Vadris, an RF-seeking payload for FPV drones that hunts ground control stations and other emitters of interest. CX2 is backed by 8VC, Point72 Ventures, Andreessen Horowitz, and others, and sells directly to military and government customers. It does not currently publish a public API or developer portal.

providers.name: DEFCON AI
providers.description: DEFCON AI is a modeling, simulation, and analysis (MS&A) company based in McLean, Virginia, building AI-driven optimization for contested logistics and mobility across defense and commercial operations. Founded in 2022, it develops mission-tailored optimization and intelligent-agent simulation products - including ARTIV (delivered to U.S. Air Force Air Mobility Command) and R-ALIGN for resilient multimodal logistics - that let planners rapidly generate and evaluate mission scenarios in dynamic, disrupted environments. The company was awarded a five-year, $115M prototype agreement supporting U.S. Marine Corps logistics modernization. DEFCON AI publishes no public API or developer platform.

providers.name: Involve Space
providers.description: Involve Space is an Italian stratospheric aerospace company building real-time Earth intelligence. It operates autonomous high-altitude balloon platforms (Stratostats) that loiter around 20 kilometers for hours, days, or weeks to deliver continuous, high-resolution Earth observation, bridging the gap between satellites, drones, and ground sensors. Its Neurostar AI flight software autonomously controls individual balloons and networks of them (LoonHive), while the CLEAR GeoAI platform turns captured imagery into geospatial insights for disaster response, infrastructure and environmental monitoring, security, and in-orbit-demonstration / payload validation. A certified B Corporation headquartered in Italy with U.S. operations at the Houston Spaceport, Involve Space is backed by Earlybird Venture Capital, CDP Venture Capital, and an EIC Accelerator grant.

providers.name: JetZero
providers.description: JetZero is a Long Beach, California aerospace company founded in 2021 by Tom O'Leary and Mark Page to bring the blended wing body (all-wing) airframe to commercial aviation. Its flagship program is the Z4, a 250-seat, international-range jetliner the company says will burn up to 50% less fuel than comparable tube-and-wing airliners, and the Jet1 full-scale demonstrator being built with Scaled Composites in Mojave, California ahead of a first flight targeted for 2027. JetZero broke ground in 2026 on a manufacturing and final-assembly campus in Greensboro, North Carolina and is opening an engineering office in Wichita, Kansas at NIAR. It is backed by the U.S. Air Force, NASA, United Airlines, Alaska Star Ventures and a $175M Series B led by B Capital, with letters of intent from Gulf Air and Japan Airlines. JetZero is an aircraft manufacturer, not a software or data provider: as of this profile it publishes no public developer portal, no API documentation, no SDKs, and no machine-readable API contract of any kind. Its public technical surface is a supplier registration and supplier standards program.

providers.name: Mach Industries
providers.description: Mach Industries develops and manufactures asymmetric aerospace and defense systems and components at scale, with a product portfolio that includes the Viper vertical-takeoff attack drone, the Glide precision strike munition, the Stratos high-altitude pseudo-satellite, the Pike long-range munition, the Dart counter-drone kinetic interceptor, and energetics testing services. Surfaced as a portfolio company of Ribbit Capital and added to the API Evangelist network. The company is a defense hardware manufacturer and publishes no public developer or API surface as of this enrichment pass.

providers.name: Orqa
providers.description: Orqa is an aerial robotics company founded in 2018 and headquartered in Osijek, Croatia, that designs and manufactures mission-ready FPV (first-person view) drone systems for the defense and enterprise markets. With full vertical integration, Orqa builds every component in-house — tactical drones such as the MRM1-5 and MRM2-10, FPV goggles (FPV.One Pilot), controllers, simulators, and detection equipment — to keep its supply chain secure and its systems high-performance. The company is ISO 9001 certified and backed by Lightspeed Venture Partners (Seed round, 2024, partners Antoine Moyroud and Alexander Schmitt). As of this profile Orqa is a hardware manufacturer and does not publish a public developer API, SDKs, or a programmatic developer surface; this repository tracks it for identity and network completeness.

providers.name: Overland AI
providers.description: Overland AI is a Seattle- and Washington, DC-based defense technology company building autonomous ground vehicle systems for military and national-security applications. Its product line spans ULTRA (a fully autonomous tactical vehicle with modular payloads), OverDrive (an off-road autonomy stack for tactical maneuver in GPS- and comms-denied environments), OverWatch (a command-and-control platform for single-operator control of multiple ground vehicles, which the company describes as offering an open API for integration with existing C2 systems), and SPARK (modular hardware that adds autonomous mobility to existing platforms). Overland AI is a portfolio company of 8VC. The company publishes no public developer portal, API reference, or OpenAPI specification; its "open API" is referenced only in marketing material and integration is handled through direct contact.

providers.name: Vermeer
providers.description: Vermeer is an American-Ukrainian defense-technology startup (founded 2018 by Brian Streem; headquartered in New York with forward operations in Kyiv) building vision-based autonomy for unmanned aerial platforms. Its Visual Positioning System (VPS) uses electro-optical and infrared cameras plus onboard AI (NVIDIA) to match imagery to 2D/3D maps and deliver precise navigation in GPS-denied, jammed, or spoofed environments. Products include Air (absolute positioning without GPS), Celestial (star-based navigation), and Terminal Guidance (precision targeting). The technology has been fielded by the Armed Forces of Ukraine and is aimed at defense customers including Lockheed Martin, General Atomics, Northrop Grumman, and the U.S. Air Force and Army. Vermeer exposes no public API, SDK, or developer platform at this time; this profile is a company/marketing surface with no API artifacts.

providers.name: 6K
providers.description: 6K Inc is a North Andover, Massachusetts advanced-materials company that produces engineered powders and battery materials with UniMelt, its patented microwave-based production-scale plasma system. Named for the roughly 6,000 K plasma temperature it operates at — the temperature of the surface of the sun — UniMelt uses tightly controlled thermal plasma beams to melt or vaporize precursor feedstock into particles with precise size distribution and crystalline phase, in seconds rather than the days conventional processes require, while cutting energy use and eliminating wastewater. The company operates through two divisions. 6K Additive, with production in Burgettstown, Pennsylvania, makes sustainably sourced metal powders for additive manufacturing — titanium Ti-6Al-4V, nickel superalloys Ni625 and Ni718, stainless SS316L, refractory tungsten, niobium C103, copper C18150 and the HEA1000 refractory alloy — reclaiming CNC scrap and revert metal into premium AM powder. 6K Energy produces domestically sourced lithium-ion battery cathode and solid-state materials including NMC, LFP, LLZO, LMO, LTO and LNMO. Additional applications span semiconductor CMP, specialty ceramics, advanced coatings, lighting and display materials, nano-engineered powders, and federal/defense programs; 6K has received US Department of Defense and Department of Energy awards for domestic critical-materials capacity. 6K is a privately held company whose shares trade on secondary markets. Enrichment probing on 2026-07-31 found no public developer API, OpenAPI/AsyncAPI/GraphQL contract, developer portal, SDK, MCP server, agent card, or event surface — 6K is a materials manufacturer, not an API provider.

providers.name: Astra Space
providers.description: Astra is a commercial space company providing dedicated small satellite launch services and flight-proven electric propulsion systems. Founded in 2016 and headquartered in Alameda, California, Astra sells two products: Launch Services on Rocket 4 — targeting roughly 600 kg to low Earth orbit at a weekly cadence — and the Astra Spacecraft Engine, a flight-proven Hall-effect electric propulsion system sold in single- and multi-thruster configurations for satellite constellations. Astra became the fastest privately funded U.S. company to reach orbit in 2021 and returned to private ownership in July 2024. Astra publishes no public developer API, SDK, or machine-readable specification; its buyer-facing surface is a set of launch-services and spacecraft-engine inquiry forms alongside a published Rocket 4 Payload User's Guide and engine data sheet.

providers.name: Cognitive Space
providers.description: Cognitive Space is an aerospace software company delivering AI-powered automated satellite operations for constellation and fleet management. Its CNTIENT.Optimize platform automates mission planning, tasking, and multi-ground-station pass scheduling for satellite operators and government agencies, reporting large per-operator time savings, while CNTIENT.Earth delivers satellite Data-as-a-Service. The company integrates with customer systems via APIs and serves clients including Terran Orbital, the Space Development Agency, the Air Force Research Lab, and NOAA. Backed by Techstars.

providers.name: Teradar
providers.description: Teradar is a Boston, Massachusetts semiconductor and sensing company founded in 2020 by Matthew Carey, Gregory Charvat and Nicholas Saiz that is commercializing terahertz-band vision sensors for vehicles, defense and security screening. Its Modular Terahertz Engine (MTE) is an all-solid-state chip architecture built from proprietary transmit (TX), receive (RX) and Teracore processing silicon, delivering 0.13-degree native angular resolution at 300+ meters in day, night, rain, fog and snow, positioned to sit alongside cameras and to displace radar and lidar in SAE L1-L5 driver assistance and autonomy programs. The company emerged from stealth in late 2025 with a $150M Series B led by VXI Capital with Ibex Investors, Capricorn Investment Group, The Engine Ventures and Lockheed Martin Ventures, and is working with global OEMs and Tier-One suppliers toward a 2028 model-year launch. Teradar is a hardware and silicon company: it publishes a marketing site and product specification sheets, but no public developer program, API, SDK, or machine-readable interface contract.

providers.name: Path Robotics
providers.description: Path Robotics is a Columbus, Ohio autonomous welding robotics company founded in 2018 by brothers Andy and Alex Lonsberry (CEO and CTO) out of Case Western Reserve University. The company builds AI-powered intelligent welding cells that automate metal fabrication for defense shipyards, utility and energy infrastructure, data centers, and heavy industry. Its core technology is Obsidian, a physical-AI reinforcement-learning agent trained inside Path's proprietary Weld World Model on tens of millions of welded inches; Obsidian runs at the edge of each cell and makes real-time, seam-by-seam welding decisions using a sensor stack of two cameras plus four lasers that deliver sub-millimeter 360-degree awareness around the torch. Path markets the cells with a CapEx-free consumption model and reports 97%+ first-pass yield, 4x productivity, and 30% lower welding costs across customers including HII (America's largest military shipbuilder), Saronic, LAD Services, Tycrop, Mine Rite Technologies, and Millerbernd. In April 2026 Path announced Rove, a mobile welding system mounted on a quadruped platform, extending its addressable geometry beyond fixed-cell applications. The company has raised approximately $271M across Seed through Series D from Drive Capital, Matter Venture Partners, Tiger Global, Addition, and Yamaha Motor Ventures, with the most recent $100M Series D closing in October 2024. Path Robotics has no public developer API, SDK, or webhook surface; its GitHub organization contains roughly 50 repositories that are almost entirely upstream open-source forks (ROS, protobuf, abseil, ceres-solver, pytorch3d, etc.) used as internal build dependencies rather than published developer artifacts. Revenue is earned through welding-cell deployments, services, and the consumable weld-output model — not API monetization.

providers.name: Cambium
providers.description: Cambium is an advanced materials company (Cambium Biomaterials, El Segundo, California, founded 2019) that molecularly re-engineers polymers from first principles, pairing AI-driven molecular design with chemistry, materials science, biology, and agile domestic manufacturing to develop and scale next-generation materials roughly 10x faster than traditional methods. Product lines span thermal protection systems, high-temperature structural polymers, and laser/directed-energy protection, serving aerospace, space, defense, motorsport, automotive, marine, and industrial customers. Its SHD Advanced Composites business runs rapid-response prepreg manufacturing across the US, UK, and EU. Backed by 8VC. Cambium publishes no public developer API, SDKs, or developer portal; this profile captures corporate identity and probed domain security only.

providers.name: Distance
providers.description: Distance (Distance Technologies) is a Helsinki-based frontier-tech company pioneering glasses-free extended reality (XR) built on computational optics and lightfield technology. Its systems turn transparent surfaces — vehicle windshields, aircraft canopies, and head-mounted visors — into intelligent heads-up displays without screens, overlays, or wearable glasses. Products include the Acuity visual-intelligence platform and Acuity OS for defense, the Field Operator HUD (FOH) head-mounted system in field trials across NATO countries, and panoramic lightfield HUDs for automotive ADAS and navigation. Distance is backed by GV (Google Ventures) and partners with defense, aerospace, and automotive organizations including Kia, Supacat, Galvion, Patria, and General Dynamics. The company publishes no public API or developer program; this profile tracks its identity and public web surface in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Northwood Space
providers.description: Northwood Space is an El Segundo, California ground-infrastructure company for the space industry, founded in 2022 by Bridgit Mendler (CEO), Griffin Cleverly (CTO), and Shaurya Luthra. It designs and delivers rapidly deployable satellite ground stations built on electronically steerable phased-array antennas that track many satellites at once with no moving parts, paired with software ("Portal") that orchestrates every contact, automates scheduling, and moves data from spacecraft to customer. Northwood aims to turn ground infrastructure into cloud-like, on-demand global capacity for defense and commercial operators. The company's software stack is described as developer-oriented with modern APIs and integration hooks, but it publishes no public developer portal, API documentation, or SDKs at this time. Backed by Andreessen Horowitz (a16z), Founders Fund, Washington Harbour Partners, and Alpine Space Ventures; raised a $100M Series B and won a $50M Space Force contract in early 2026.

providers.name: Oshkosh
providers.description: Oshkosh Corporation is a Fortune 500 industrial company that designs and builds purpose-built vehicles and vehicle bodies, including access equipment, defense vehicles, fire and emergency apparatus, refuse collection vehicles, and concrete mixers.

providers.name: United States Africa Command
providers.description: United States Africa Command (AFRICOM) is a unified combatant command of the United States Department of Defense responsible for military operations and coordination in Africa. AFRICOM's primary mission is to advance U.S. national security interests and promote regional stability through security cooperation, military assistance, and joint training exercises with African partner nations. AFRICOM is headquartered at Kelley Barracks in Stuttgart, Germany and maintains relationships with 53 African nations. The command is led by a four-star general and conducts operations spanning humanitarian assistance, counter-terrorism, peacekeeping support, and capacity-building activities across the continent.

providers.name: Isengard Industries Inc
providers.description: Isengard Industries builds sovereign production capability for defense: the means for allied nations to manufacture precision-strike and counter-drone (counter-UAS) systems by the thousand, on their own soil, at a fraction of what traditional prime contractors charge. The company describes its approach as "Weapons of Mass Production." Founded in 2026 and part of Y Combinator's Summer 2026 batch, it is led by Francisco Serra-Martins (previously co-founder/CEO of Terminal Autonomy) and James Tennant (former Australian Army officer), and is headquartered in San Francisco. As a hardware and defense-manufacturing company it does not currently publish a public developer API, SDKs, or API documentation; this profile captures its public identity and security surface for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Firestorm
providers.description: Firestorm (Firestorm Labs, Inc.) is a San Diego based defense technology company founded in 2022 that builds expeditionary manufacturing systems and modular unmanned aerial systems. Its xCELL containerized production unit uses HP Multi Jet Fusion additive manufacturing to 3D print industrial-grade PA-12 nylon composite airframes and spare parts at the tactical edge, feeding modular UAS platforms including the Tempest fixed-wing family and the Squall FPV drone.
