The company holds a five-year, $100M U.S. Air Force IDIQ and closed an $82M Series B in April 2026 led by Washington Harbour Partners. Firestorm ships hardware, not software: as of this profiling pass it publishes no developer portal, no public API, and no machine-readable API contract.

providers.name: L3Harris Technologies
providers.description: L3Harris Technologies is an agile global aerospace and defense technology innovator delivering end-to-end solutions in space, air, land, sea, and cyber domains for government and commercial customers. No publicly documented APIs are available; product integrations are delivered through customer engagements.

providers.name: Moog
providers.description: Moog Inc. is a worldwide designer, manufacturer, and integrator of precision motion and fluid control products and solutions for aerospace, defense, industrial, and medical applications. Product divisions include actuation, motion systems, motors, propulsion, valves, aerospace components, and defense systems. Moog does not currently publish a public developer API or developer portal.

providers.name: GATE Space
providers.description: GATE Space is an Austrian aerospace company redefining in-space mobility with high-thrust chemical propulsion systems for satellites, capsules, and landing vehicles. A TU Wien spinout founded in 2022 and backed by Techstars, the company builds the GATE Jetpack — a plug-and-play, refuelable propulsion module running on green propellants that lets satellites perform rapid orbit and attitude maneuvers with no integration effort. Its patented engines have been validated across 8,000+ hot-fire tests in atmospheric and vacuum conditions, manufactured in a European facility with a 98% local supply chain. GATE Space raised €6.3M via the EIC Accelerator and its propulsion system will fly on BeaconSat, Austria's first military satellite. This is a hardware manufacturer with no public developer/API surface; the profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network as a company identity record.

providers.name: Kela Technologies
providers.description: Kela Technologies (kela.io) is a defense technology company founded by veterans of elite Israeli intelligence units, providing a secure, open platform that enables rapid and seamless integration of commercial and military systems in service of Western defense. The company emerged from stealth in 2025 after raising $39M from Sequoia Capital, Lux Capital, and In-Q-Tel (the CIA's venture arm). Kela is building "Sovereign Sky," a low-Earth-orbit satellite constellation for resilient communication and navigation independent of foreign infrastructure, and acquired cloud-management company Pelanor. As of this enrichment pass the company publishes a single-page marketing site with a privacy policy but no public API, developer portal, documentation, or machine-readable interface.

providers.name: Pyka
providers.description: Pyka is an Alameda, California company that designs and manufactures large, dual-use heavy-lift autonomous electric aircraft for commercial and defense operations. Its flagship products are the Pelican 2 autonomous crop-protection aircraft for aerial application and the DropShip long-range heavy-lift cargo UAS. Pyka builds a fully integrated, vertically owned autonomy stack — an Autonomy Engine (real-time OS, sensor fusion, flight control, and path planning), a Mission Control operator suite (simulation, communications, and operator interface), and custom aerospace-grade hardware. The company is backed by DCVC and Obvious Ventures. Pyka does not currently publish a public developer API, SDK, or developer portal; this profile captures its public web and domain-security footprint. Surfaced via VC portfolio enrichment.

providers.name: Rebellion Defense
providers.description: Rebellion Defense (rebelliondefense.com) is a defense-technology company building an AI-driven "intelligence shield" for protecting critical infrastructure and military assets — combining multi-band AESA radar sensing (ARGUS/SPECTRUM), AI track-fusion and threat prediction (PRISM), operator alerting and situational awareness (IRIS/STATUS), and effector command-and-control (HADES) on an integrated RBLN-OS platform. Recent public activity includes U.S. Navy contracts and designation as an awardable vendor on the CDAO Tradewinds Solutions Marketplace. The company publishes a marketing site only: as of this enrichment pass no public API, developer portal, SDKs, or machine-readable discovery surface is exposed. Added to the API Evangelist network as an Insight Partners portfolio lead.

providers.name: Astro Mechanica
providers.description: Astro Mechanica is a San Francisco aerospace company, founded in 2021 by Ian Brooke, reinventing supersonic flight for a new jet age. Its flagship Duality electric combined-cycle engine is engineered to stay efficient from takeoff through Mach 3+ by reconfiguring between turbofan, turbojet, and ramjet modes using a hybrid turboelectric architecture. The company designs engines, airframes, and flight systems in-house, has been selected to develop an engine for the U.S. Air Force Collaborative Combat Aircraft (CCA) program, and is backed by a16z, Lowercarbon Capital, and Y Combinator. It was added to the API Evangelist network as an a16z portfolio company. As an aerospace hardware manufacturer, Astro Mechanica publishes no public developer API, SDK, or developer portal; this profile captures the company's public web and identity surface only.

providers.name: Carpenter Technology
providers.description: Carpenter Technology Corporation is a U.S.-based producer and distributor of premium specialty alloys — including titanium alloys, powder metals, high-temperature stainless steels, tool steels, and soft magnetic alloys — serving the aerospace, defense, medical, transportation, energy, and industrial end markets. The company supports customers through technical product resources such as its Alloy Finder, alloy technical data sheets, conversion tables, and a member-only Customer Portal for order and account self-service, but does not currently publish a public developer API.

providers.name: Rolls-Royce
providers.description: Rolls-Royce plc is a British multinational aerospace and defense company manufacturing aero engines (Trent series), defense propulsion, and power systems. Rolls-Royce does not publish a public developer API. The company operates supplier portals at suppliers.rolls-royce.com and maintains a small GitHub presence with the qc-cfd open-source repository covering quantum computing for computational fluid dynamics research.

providers.name: LINSOL Co.,Ltd.
providers.description: LINSOL Co.,Ltd. (린솔) is a safety-technology company headquartered in Daejeon, South Korea, founded as an in-house venture spun out of Hanwha Aerospace. LINSOL adapts acoustic detection techniques originally developed for defense landmine applications into commercial real-time hazard, accident, and environmental detection. Its product line includes Karang F (driving-environment detection), Karang S (precision acoustic signal transmission), SkyShield (fall detection), BR, Acoustic Eye (aerial security), and Safety Nova (smart integrated safety platform), sold into industrial safety, ESG, and defense security use cases. The company operates a Daejeon headquarters and research center plus a Goheung branch. LINSOL ships hardware and integrated platforms; as of a 2026-07-19 probe it publishes no public developer API, portal, SDK, or machine-readable specification.

providers.name: Quantum Space
providers.description: Quantum Space is a space defense and orbital mobility company headquartered in Rockville, Maryland, building Ranger — a maneuverable spacecraft designed to operate across LEO, MEO, GEO and cislunar orbits. Per the company's own published material, Ranger carries up to 4,000 kg of storable propellant, uses multi-mode chemical and electric propulsion for up to 12 km/s of delta-V, is designed for a 15-year on-station operational life, supports on-orbit refueling in both directions, and exposes a modular five-port payload architecture. The company sells space domain awareness, satellite servicing, satellite life extension and on-orbit refueling to national security, civil and commercial customers, with engineering in Rockville, propulsion and integration in Hawthorne, California and Huntsville, Alabama, and spacecraft production in Tulsa, Oklahoma. Leadership includes CEO Jim Bridenstine (former NASA Administrator), Executive Chairman Kam Ghaffarian and President Kerry Wisnosky. Quantum Space publishes no public developer program, API reference or machine-readable API contract; the only machine-readable artifact served from its own hosts is an llms.txt at the website root.

providers.name: Arctus Aerospace
providers.description: Arctus Aerospace is a Bengaluru, India based deep-tech startup building high-altitude, long-endurance autonomous unmanned aircraft (MALE/HALE UAVs) for real-time Earth observation and geospatial intelligence. Its platforms are designed to operate near 45,000 feet for over 24 hours while carrying payloads up to 250 kg, delivering centimeter-level multispectral imagery as a "zero-infrastructure" alternative to satellites. The company positions itself as a data-as-a-service provider, selling subscription-based aerial coverage for energy, infrastructure, climate, defense, and agriculture use cases. Founded in 2024 by Shreepoorna S. Rao, Arctus raised a $2.6M pre-seed round led by Version One Ventures (with South Park Commons, gradCapital, and angels). As of this writing the company is pre-product from an API standpoint and publishes no public developer surface, API, or documentation; this profile was surfaced as a Version One Ventures portfolio lead.

providers.name: Atlas Motion Systems
providers.description: Atlas Motion Systems (atlasmotion.com) designs and builds brushless DC (BLDC) motors and actuators for defense and robotics applications, engineered around a customer's specific program and manufactured at scale. The public web presence is a single-page marketing site (hero plus a contact page); it is a hardware company that does not publish a developer portal, public API, SDKs, documentation, or well-known discovery surface. This profile was seeded as a Homebrew-portfolio lead and enriched with verifiable identity and live domain-security probe data only. Enrichment found no API surface to harvest.

providers.name: Heaviside Industries
providers.description: Heaviside Industries is a defense-technology company founded in 2024 in Los Angeles, California, building autonomous precision munitions for U.S. and allied special operations and conventional forces. Its products — MOTH (land electromagnetic signal intelligence and spectrum awareness), TYR (autonomous aerial munition), and HYDRA (autonomous underwater munition) — are designed to deliver hyper-precise strike capabilities across air, land, and sea in GPS-denied and contested environments. Named after physicist Oliver Heaviside, whose electromagnetic theory enabled miniaturized electronics, the company emerged from stealth in May 2026 with a $28M Series A. It does not currently publish a public API, developer portal, SDKs, or machine-readable API artifacts.

providers.name: Seeing Systems
providers.description: Seeing Systems is a Y Combinator (Winter 2026) defense technology company building autonomous, modular strike drones and AI-powered swarm coordination software at the intersection of artificial intelligence and robotics. Its product line includes Bandit, a cost-effective FPV drone for training and expendable missions with 30+ km of range; Banshee, an autonomous modular platform built for contested, jamming-resistant environments with 40+ km of range; and Aerie AI, swarm coordination software for multi-platform operations that lowers operator cognitive load. The company works directly with military and defense partners — including UK Royal Marine Commandos and NATO forces — rather than publishing a public developer platform. This profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network; as of the latest enrichment pass Seeing Systems exposes no public API, SDK, developer portal, or documentation surface.

providers.name: VICTUS Technologies
providers.description: VICTUS Technologies builds contested-autonomy software for autonomous systems operating in GPS-denied and jamming-heavy environments. Its PhantomNAV platform delivers precise state estimation from the gravity and inertial sensors already embedded in drones, aircraft, submarines, satellites, and ships - no new hardware required - and integrates with Palantir Foundry's AIP infrastructure. VICTUS is backed by Techstars and added to the API Evangelist network. The company publishes a marketing and platform site but exposes no public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface at this time.

providers.name: Leidos
providers.description: Leidos, a Fortune 500 digital and mission innovator, delivers solutions at the intersection of national security, health, and critical infrastructure. With a global workforce of approximately 47,000, the company is executing its NorthStar 2030 strategy focused on five growth engines: space and maritime, energy infrastructure, digital modernization and cyber, mission software, and managed health. No public REST APIs or developer portal have been identified.

providers.name: Muon Space
providers.description: Muon Space is a Mountain View, California-based end-to-end space systems company that designs, builds, and operates mission-optimized satellite constellations to deliver Earth Intelligence and enable real-time compute and decision-making in space. Founded in 2021 by veterans of Skybox, NASA, and SpaceX, the company's core product is Muon Halo, an integrated technology stack composed of MuSim (constellation simulation and digital twin), MuOS (IP-based software-defined network middleware connecting space, ground, and cloud), MuCore (software-configurable instrument core), Condor (modular Condor-M and Condor-XL spacecraft platforms), and MuDash (cloud-based tasking, scheduling, and operations dashboard). Muon Space's flagship public mission is FireSat, a purpose-built wildfire detection and monitoring constellation developed with the Earth Fire Alliance, Google Research, and the Gordon & Betty Moore Foundation; FireSat carries a high-dynamic-range multispectral IR instrument capable of detecting 5x5 meter fires across a 1,500 km swath with a 50 m nadir ground sample distance, with revisit times targeted to twenty minutes once the full constellation is operational. The Protoflight satellite produced its first-light imagery in June 2025, with the first block of three additional satellites launching in 2026 and full operational capacity targeted for 2030. Other Muon Space missions support the U.S. Air Force and U.S. Space Force for next-generation weather monitoring, Hydrosat for thermal geospatial intelligence in climate and agriculture, and global security applications including missile-defense architecture. Muon Space's revenue model is mission contracting, spacecraft and constellation delivery, and hosted data services; there is no public developer API, SDK, or open-source release of the Halo platform or FireSat data feed.

providers.name: TTM Technologies
providers.description: TTM Technologies, Inc. (NASDAQ: TTMI) is a leading global manufacturer of technology products, including mission systems, radio frequency components, RF microwave and microelectronic assemblies, and technologically advanced printed circuit boards (PCBs). TTM serves aerospace and defense, data center computing, medical, industrial and instrumentation, automotive, and networking and communications markets. The company reported approximately $2.9B in FY2025 revenue, operates 24 specialized facilities across North America and Asia Pacific, and employs more than 18,000 people. TTM expanded its defense electronics footprint with the 2022 acquisition of Telephonics from Griffon Corporation.

providers.name: Aethero
providers.description: Aethero designs and manufactures radiation-hardened, space-rated edge computing systems and AI/ML software for satellites, space stations, and orbital data centers, enabling autonomous on-orbit processing of imagery and sensor data rather than downlinking raw feeds. Its NVIDIA Jetson Orin/Thor-based NxN-ECM and NxA-ECM edge computing modules, Titan and Phobos platforms, the Aether fleet-management software framework, and the AMATDT model annotation/training/deployment tool let spacecraft run AI inference in orbit. Founded in 2023 and headquartered in San Francisco, Aethero raised an $8.4M seed round led by Kindred Ventures in June 2025. Aethero exposes no public web API today; this profile captures the company's identity and its live domain-security posture for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Arlo Industries
providers.description: Arlo Industries is a San Francisco defense hardware company (Y Combinator, Spring 2026) building a passive sensing network for detecting and tracking drones and aerial threats without traditional radar. Its product, Mentat, uses a distributed mesh architecture of low-cost sensors that cooperatively detect and track targets in 3D while remaining invisible to the threats they monitor. The company frames its approach around "asymmetric economics" — sensor deployment cost grows linearly while tracking accuracy grows exponentially — making the system more scalable than conventional radar installations. Arlo has demonstrated its technology with Ukrainian military operators on active frontlines and maintains partnerships across the US, Ukraine, and Northern Europe. As an early-stage hardware startup it publishes no public API, developer program, or SDKs at this time.

providers.name: BlackSky
providers.description: BlackSky Technology (NYSE: BKSY) is a Herndon, Virginia headquartered real-time space-based intelligence company that operates a high-revisit Earth observation constellation and delivers AI-enhanced tactical ISR (intelligence, surveillance, and reconnaissance) imagery and analytics to defense, intelligence, and global security customers. BlackSky's flagship product is the Spectra platform — a cloud-based intelligence hub that provides on-demand satellite tasking, sub-90-minute imagery delivery, automated AI-driven object detection and change monitoring, archived imagery access, and a secure tasking and delivery API. The company operates Gen-2 satellites at 83 cm resolution and a newer Gen-3 constellation delivering 35 cm class very-high-resolution imagery with infrared sensors, inter-satellite links, and on-board AI processing, manufactured at BlackSky's facility in Tukwila, Washington. Commercial offerings include BlackSky ON-DEMAND (flexible global tasking) and BlackSky ASSURED (dedicated, contracted persistent monitoring capacity). BlackSky's Spectra tasking and imagery API is integrated into partner platforms including Esri ArcGIS, UP42, and the STAT (Satellite Tasking API) community spec, however the API is access-controlled for vetted defense, intelligence, and enterprise customers and is not exposed as a public self-service developer portal — there is no public Spectra developer documentation site, OpenAPI specification, or open SDKs at the time of this entry. The customer revenue model is subscription-based Spectra ON-DEMAND and ASSURED contracts, Mission Solutions custom engagements, and through marketplace partners.

providers.name: BlueYard
providers.description: BlueYard Capital is a venture capital firm founded in 2016, operating as a small, equal partnership with offices in Europe and the United States. Managing roughly $500M in AUM, it invests $500K-$5M at pre-seed to Series A as lead or co-lead investor, backing two kinds of technologies: those that move us toward utopia and those that hold the line against oblivion. Its focus areas span computation & intelligence, engineering/aerospace & defense, biology & chemistry, and crypto. Notable portfolio companies and exits include Privy (acquired by Stripe), Groq, IonQ, Filecoin, Castelion, and Marvel Fusion. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio relationship of foundry-group and enriched from BlueYard's public website; it exposes no public developer API.

providers.name: Constelli
providers.description: Constelli (Constelli Signals Private Limited) is a Hyderabad, India based defence and aerospace signal-processing company founded in 2017 by Satya Gopal Panigrahi and Avinash Chenreddy. It designs and manufactures radar systems, radar target and echo simulators, deployable drone-based radar payloads, high-performance radar processors, and IRIG-standard digital telemetry receivers for ground, onboard, and satellite telemetry. Its products serve electronic warfare and defence R&D programs globally, including India's Ministry of Defence and DRDO. Constelli raised a $20M Series A led by General Catalyst (with Pravega Ventures and 360 One). It is a hardware/systems company and does not currently publish a public developer API, portal, or SDKs.

providers.name: Fortastra
providers.description: Fortastra is a spacecraft manufacturer building low-cost, maneuverable orbital defense systems designed for scalability and autonomous operation. Its spacecraft protect space-based infrastructure with autonomous navigation that detects, analyzes, and responds to orbital anomalies without relying on distant ground-based sensors. The company's open software architecture spans sensing, maneuvering, coordination, and response functions, and its hardware is validated through component testing, simulation, and orbital deployment. Surfaced as a portfolio company of bloomberg-beta.

providers.name: Hermeus
providers.description: Hermeus is an American aerospace and defense company building rapidly reusable high-Mach and hypersonic aircraft for national-security missions in partnership with the U.S. Department of Defense. Founded in 2018 and headquartered in Atlanta, Georgia, the company applies a hardware-rich, rapid design-build-test approach to move quickly from concept to flight. Its programs include Quarterhorse, a reusable high-speed flight-test aircraft; Darkhorse, a multi-mission reusable hypersonic uncrewed aerial system (UAS); and Chimera, a hybrid turbine-based combined-cycle engine that transitions from turbojet takeoff through supersonic flight into hypersonic acceleration. Hermeus is a hardware manufacturer with no public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface; this profile tracks the company's public web, security, and corporate properties in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Inversion
providers.description: Inversion is a Los Angeles-based aerospace and defense company founded in 2021 by Austin Briggs and Justin Fiaschetti, building a new class of highly maneuverable reentry vehicles. Its flagship Arc is an autonomous, reusable, low-cost space-based delivery vehicle designed to store cargo in orbit and deliver it with precision to anywhere on Earth in under an hour, descending under parachutes using non-toxic propellants so crews can approach it immediately on landing. The company also develops hypersonics and space-based interceptor technology and flew its first reentry capsule, Ray, as an early technical demonstrator. Inversion has raised roughly $54M to date, including a $44M Series A led by Spark Capital and Adjacent with participation from Lockheed Martin Ventures, Kindred Ventures, and Y Combinator. It does not currently publish a public developer API; this profile tracks the company for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Inversion Space
providers.description: Inversion Space is a Los Angeles-based aerospace and defense company founded in 2021 by Justin Fiaschetti and Austin Briggs, building autonomous, reusable, and low-cost reentry vehicles that turn space into a global logistics network. Its Arc vehicle is designed to store cargo in orbit and deliver a 500-pound payload to anywhere on Earth in under an hour, while its first spacecraft, Ray, validated key reentry subsystems. The company also develops hypersonic test capabilities and space-based interceptor technology, partnering with Anduril on the Golden Dome program and Kratos on the MACH-TB 2.0 hypersonic test program, backed by a $71M U.S. Space Force contract. It is in the API Evangelist network as a company profile; no public developer API, documentation, or SDK surface was found during enrichment.

providers.name: MightyFly
providers.description: MightyFly is an autonomous air-logistics company building hybrid-electric eVTOL cargo aircraft for expedited, long-range, same-day deliveries. Its autonomous aircraft carry up to 500 pounds, travel up to 1,000 miles at roughly 150 MPH, and cut delivery emissions by around 64% versus traditional ground and air freight. MightyFly targets B2B logistics and defense delivery partnerships rather than offering a public developer platform. As of this enrichment pass the company publishes no developer API, SDK, developer portal, or public specifications; this profile captures its public web presence and probed domain-security posture.

providers.name: Quantum Systems
providers.description: Quantum-Systems GmbH is a Gilching/Munich, Germany-based dual-use drone manufacturer founded in 2015 by former Bundeswehr helicopter pilot Florian Seibel. The company designs, builds, and operates small electric vertical take-off and landing (eVTOL) fixed-wing unmanned aircraft systems (UAS) for reconnaissance, intelligence, surveillance, target acquisition (RSTA), surveying, and mapping. Its flagship platforms include the Trinity Pro (mapping/surveying VTOL with up to 90-minute endurance), the Vector tactical reconnaissance drone (the de facto main small UAS supplier to the German Bundeswehr and, with 619+ systems delivered as of April 2025, one of the most-used Western reconnaissance drones in Ukraine), the Reliant long-range Group 2 ISR/RSTA platform built for the U.S. market with 10+ hours endurance and hot-swappable MOD-compliant payload bays (EO/IR, SIGINT, EW, CRPA), and the Ukraine-manufactured Sparta drone carrier that delivers two FPV drones to a 200 km combat radius. All platforms are operated through QBase 3D, Quantum-Systems' proprietary Windows-based mission planning, control, and post-processing software with integrated ESRI terrain data and direct export to Pix4D, Agisoft, Propeller, and Trimble Business Center. The Vector tactical line is built on Auterion's flight stack. Backed by HV Capital, DTCP, Thiel Capital, Project A, Airbus Ventures, and Omnes Capital, the company reached unicorn status in May 2025 as "Europe's first dual-use unicorn." Quantum-Systems supplies the militaries of Germany, the United States, Ukraine, Australia, the Netherlands, New Zealand, Romania, and Spain. There is no public developer API, REST endpoint, SDK, or open-source release for QBase 3D or any Quantum-Systems platform; integration with Pix4D/Agisoft/Propeller/Trimble is via standard photogrammetry file exchange (GeoTIFF, RAW imagery, flight logs), not a programmable API.

providers.name: Shift5
providers.description: Shift5 is an operational technology (OT) cyber and observability company that instruments the onboard serial data buses of planes, trains, and military weapons systems to deliver real-time intrusion detection, predictive maintenance, and compliance intelligence for defense and transportation fleets. Founded by former US Army Cyber Command engineers, it collects and analyzes data directly from vehicle bus networks (MIL-STD-1553, ARINC 429, CAN) to give operators actionable insight into the health and security of their platforms. Backed by Insight Partners. This profile was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio-lead stub; enrichment confirms Shift5 publishes no public API or developer program.

providers.name: Spirit AeroSystems Holdings
providers.description: Spirit AeroSystems Holdings is one of the world's largest manufacturers of aerostructures for commercial airplanes, defense platforms, and business and regional jets. Spirit designs and builds fuselages, pylons, nacelles, and wing components for major aircraft programs including Boeing 737 MAX, 787, and Airbus A350. The company does not publicly expose developer APIs; its digital operations are focused on internal supply chain, manufacturing execution, and enterprise systems.

providers.name: Tekever
providers.description: Tekever is a multinational defence technology company headquartered in Lisbon, Portugal, with operations in the United Kingdom (Bath and a planned large-scale drone production facility in Swindon), France (Toulouse and Cahors), and the United States (Fayetteville, North Carolina). Founded in 2001, the company specialises in AI-driven autonomy for civil and defence missions, with its core business centred on long-endurance Unmanned Aerial Systems (UAS) used for Intelligence, Surveillance, and Reconnaissance (ISR), maritime surveillance, and electronic warfare. Its flagship platforms include the AR3, a configurable medium-range tactical UAS (designated StormShroud in service with the UK Royal Air Force), the AR5, a SATCOM-enabled long-endurance maritime and land ISR aircraft, and the ARX, a next-generation system positioned as the company's game changer. These platforms are paired with ATLAS, Tekever's real-time intelligence-as-a-service platform that fuses sensor and satellite data into actionable mission intelligence. Tekever drones are operated by the UK Ministry of Defence, the British Army, the Armed Forces of Ukraine (with the UK having committed approximately £270 million in Tekever UAVs for Ukraine since the start of the Russian invasion), the European Maritime Safety Agency under a €30 million contract, the French Ministry of Armed Forces (CNES/DGA), Portugal, and NATO. The company also develops satellite technology and Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) capabilities to extend its intelligence services beyond the airborne domain. Tekever's revenue model is built on government and defence contracts, platform sales, and managed ISR-as-a-service offerings; it does not publish a public developer API, SDK, or open-source release, and engagement with the company is conducted through direct sales, government procurement, and partnership channels.

providers.name: Vulcan Elements
providers.description: Vulcan Elements is a United States manufacturer of sintered permanent neodymium-iron-boron (NdFeB) rare earth magnets, founded in 2023 and headquartered in Research Triangle Park, North Carolina. The company produces high-performance rare earth magnets domestically for defense and commercial applications — the components that convert electricity into motion in motors, drones, robotics, vehicles and consumer electronics — as an alternative to a supply chain concentrated in China. In 2025 it announced a $65 million Series A, a $620 million loan from the Pentagon's Office of Strategic Capital, and a $1.4 billion partnership with the U.S. government and ReElement Technologies to build a vertically integrated domestic magnet supply chain, including a nearly $1 billion, 1,000-job magnet factory in Benson, Johnston County, North Carolina. Vulcan Elements is a physical-goods manufacturer: it publishes no public API, developer portal, SDK or machine-readable specification.

providers.name: Firehawk Aerospace
providers.description: Firehawk Aerospace, Inc. is a Dallas, Texas defense-technology manufacturer founded in 2019 by Ronald Jones, Will Edwards and Steve Edwards that replaces conventional rocket-propulsion production with additive manufacturing. Its proprietary 3D-printed solid rocket fuel, branded 3D-Ultra, is used to build hybrid rocket engines and solid rocket motors whose fuel-grain geometry is printed rather than cast, cutting production timelines from years to weeks while removing the handling hazards of traditional energetics. The company works under U.S. Army Applications Laboratory SBIR Phase III and U.S. Air Force Test Center contracts, has flight-tested an additively manufactured GMLRS-class analog, and is expanding manufacturing capacity in Lawton, Oklahoma and Crawford, Mississippi. Firehawk now operates publicly as Firehawk Defense (firehawkdefense.com); the firehawkaerospace.com domain 301-redirects there. It is a hardware and energetics manufacturer, not a software vendor: it publishes no developer portal, no API documentation, no SDK and no machine-readable API contract.

providers.name: AICE
providers.description: AICE is a defense-technology company building the next generation of underwater defense systems: autonomous swarms of modular marine drones that secure naval assets and coastal infrastructure against evolving underwater threats. Founded in 2026 by former NASA engineer Gregoire Chomette and European Robotics Champion Remi Bouteiller, the company is part of the Y Combinator Spring 2026 batch, is based in the San Francisco Bay Area with hardware manufactured in France, and applies swarm robotics and AI to surveillance, detection, and protection of critical subsea infrastructure. AICE currently ships hardware and does not publish a public API, SDK, or developer platform; this profile tracks the company for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Booz Allen Hamilton
providers.description: Booz Allen Hamilton is a leading management and technology consulting firm providing services primarily to U.S. government agencies in defense, intelligence, and civil markets. The firm employs over 2,500 AI specialists and 8,000 cybersecurity professionals, and maintains a significant open source presence on GitHub with projects including the Solutions Delivery Platform, Open Data Platform, and Cognition data fusion platform.

providers.name: Foundation Robotics Labs
providers.description: Foundation Robotics Labs — trading publicly as Foundation and incorporated as Foundation Future Industries, Inc. — is a San Francisco humanoid robotics company founded in April 2024 by Sankaet Pathak, Arjun Sethi and Mike LeBlanc. It builds Phantom, a general-purpose humanoid robot aimed at industrial automation, logistics, inspection, disaster response and defense, and Cortex, the company's self-described physics foundation model built on Deep Variational Bayes Filters that pairs physics-informed prediction with vision-language reasoning to drive the robot. The company's published master plan runs from building humanoids through fleet coherence and on to building cities, and it states explicitly that it designs for military environments, unlike U.S. competitors committed to non-weaponization. Foundation has raised a reported $111M and is traded on the secondary market via Forge Global. As of this profile Foundation publishes NO public developer surface — no developer portal, documentation, API reference, OpenAPI/AsyncAPI definition, SDK, package, MCP server or agent card. Its entire public web presence is a five-page Framer marketing site (home, Phantom, Cortex, master plan, culture, careers) with no /docs, /developers, /api, /pricing, /terms or /privacy paths and no llms.txt. Its GitHub organization (github.com/foundationbot, verified first-party by @foundation.bot commit-author domains) holds internal test benches and forks of open-source robotics tooling — Drake, jetson-containers, Kalibr, PlotJuggler, Fast-DDS, an EtherCAT master, actuator dyno benches and NXP S32K MCU demos — and contains no API specification of any kind.

providers.name: NODA AI
providers.description: NODA AI is a defense-technology company building autonomous force orchestration for the frontlines. Founded in 2024 in Austin, Texas by Global War on Terrorism veterans, it develops URZA, an AI-native strategic orchestration platform that acts as a tactics repository and reasoning engine for real-time task brokering across vendor-agnostic, mixed-fleet autonomous assets, integrated with 30+ OEM vehicles and control systems from subsurface to space; and LARIA, a synthetic weapons-and-tactics training environment that uses digital-twin modeling to develop and test autonomous plays. In February 2026 the company raised a $25M Series A led by Bessemer Venture Partners to serve the U.S. Department of War, the Intelligence Community, and the UK Ministry of Defense. NODA AI is a portfolio company of Bessemer Venture Partners and Bloomberg Beta. It publishes no public API, developer documentation, or SDKs; its GitHub organization holds no public repositories.

providers.name: ThayerMahan
providers.description: ThayerMahan, Inc. is a U.S. maritime autonomy and ocean-intelligence company headquartered in Groton, Connecticut, founded in 2016 and led by former U.S. Navy Vice Admiral Michael Connor. It builds and operates uncrewed surface and subsurface sensing systems — Outpost, SeaPicket, SeaGuard (a non-kinetic counter-UUV defeat system) and the TransparenSea data platform — combining passive acoustic arrays, electronic sensors, edge processing, AI classification and human analysts to deliver persistent undersea surveillance, port and critical-infrastructure security, subsea infrastructure monitoring, passive acoustic marine-mammal monitoring and illegal-fishing (IUU) detection for defense, government and commercial offshore customers. ThayerMahan sells outcomes as a service rather than developer tooling: it publishes no developer portal, no API documentation and no machine-readable contract. The only public reference to programmatic access is on the TransparenSea page, which states that contact reports are delivered by application programming interface (API), voice report, or other means in near real-time — a customer-delivery integration negotiated per engagement, not a self-serve public API. Its GitHub organization holds two forks of third-party tools and no first-party libraries.

providers.name: Valinor
providers.description: Valinor Enterprises is a defense and government technology operational holding company — a "company of companies" that builds and buys mission-critical technologies to fill the gaps others ignore. It centralizes go-to-market, compliance, security, and operations while decentralizing engineering across lean Product Companies including Condor (attritable aerial systems), Dispatch (drone charging infrastructure, selected by DIU for the CADDS program), Harbor (expeditionary medical systems for the Marine Corps), Reflex (smart optics with onboard vision models), and Streamline (AI-enabled data collection with structured ontology write-back). Backed by General Catalyst; raised a $54M Series A led by Friends & Family Capital. Valinor publishes no public API or developer portal; its developer footprint is a GitHub organization and the @valinor-enterprises npm scope.

providers.name: PowerLight Technologies
providers.description: PowerLight Technologies is an American engineering company headquartered in Kent, Washington that develops laser power beaming systems — wireless transmission of kilowatt-level electrical power over free space and over optical fiber. Founded as LaserMotive and renamed in 2017, the company builds power-over-fiber and free-space laser power links for defense unmanned aerial systems, telecom sites, temporary and disaster power, smart-grid applications, and lunar and satellite power distribution, including work under DARPA's LunA-10 program. Its products are hardware energy-transmission systems rather than software, and the company publishes no public developer program, API, or machine-readable API contract.

providers.name: Radia
providers.description: Radia is a dual-use aerospace company founded in 2016 by MIT-trained aerospace engineer Mark Lundstrom, headquartered in Boulder, Colorado with a second operating base in Italy led by Giuseppe Giordo. After roughly seven years in stealth the company emerged in March 2024 with WindRunner, an aircraft it describes as the largest ever built: roughly ten times the cargo volume of a Boeing 777, sized to carry onshore wind turbine blades of up to about 105 metres, and designed to land on semi-prepared packed-dirt or gravel strips so that oversized cargo can be flown directly to a wind farm, a forward operating site or a disaster zone rather than trucked over highways it cannot fit on. Radia frames WindRunner as a deliberately low-novelty airframe assembled from existing certified technologies to shorten the certification path, targeting entry into service in the early 2030s across three markets: energy (delivering the very large blades that make low-wind onshore sites economic), defense (outsized-volume strategic airlift), and commercial supply-chain logistics. It has assembled an industrial ecosystem of more than twenty suppliers and technology partners including Aernnova, Leonardo, AFuzion, Atitech, Latecoere, Stirling Dynamics, Collier Aerospace and Maximus Air, and has raised roughly USD 128 million from investors including ConocoPhillips, Lauder Partners, LS Power Development and HCVC. Radia is an aircraft manufacturer and logistics operator rather than a software vendor: as of August 2026 it publishes no developer portal, no API documentation, no SDK and no machine-readable API contract of any kind. Its only machine-readable public surface is the Strapi headless-CMS backend at radia.com/strapi that renders its own marketing site, whose content API is permission-locked and undocumented.

providers.name: 9 Mothers Corporation
providers.description: 9 Mothers Corporation is a defense technology company founded in 2024 and based in Austin, Texas, building AI-powered counter-drone (C-sUAS) point defense systems for the FPV drone era. Its flagship product, EDDA, is a small, low-power, autonomous-capable point-defense turret that engages Group 1 suicide drones at 10-100+ meter range to protect soldiers, vehicles, and critical assets. A Y Combinator Spring 2026 company with reported sales to the U.S. Department of War, its roadmap includes Vor (passive acoustic sensor), Atla (belt-fed shotgun system), and Gleipnir (counter-drone for larger platforms). This profile was surfaced as a Y Combinator portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network. The company publishes no public API, SDK, or developer portal.

providers.name: Amca
providers.description: Amca (Advanced Manufacturing Company of America) is an El Segundo, California aerospace and defense manufacturer rebuilding America's industrial base by acquiring specialized component suppliers and expanding competition and capacity for critical parts — actuators, switches, hydraulics, pressure sensors, power electronics, and flight-control electronics. Founded in 2024 by Eli Giovanetti and Jai Malik, Amca combines design, testing, and production into a single RAPID platform across a network of AS9100D-certified factories (Electro-Mech Components, Electrocube, Aerospace Control Products, Payne Magnetics, Cal-Draulics, BC Power Systems), and serves nearly every major aerospace and defense prime and Tier 1 supplier — Boeing, Lockheed Martin, Airbus, GE Aerospace, Honeywell, Textron, BAE Systems, and the Defense Logistics Agency. It is a hardware manufacturing company with no public developer API surface.

providers.name: American Aerospace Advisors
providers.description: American Aerospace Technologies, Inc., doing business as American Aerospace Advisors, is a defense and critical-infrastructure monitoring company based in Conshohocken, Pennsylvania. It provides end-to-end airborne intelligence systems that combine unmanned aircraft systems (UAS), airborne sensors, analytics, and communications to deliver near-real-time data through a cloud-based intelligence gateway. Its flagship AiRanger medium-altitude long-endurance unmanned aircraft and InstiMaps sensor technology support pipeline and linear-asset patrol, beyond-visual-line-of-sight (BVLOS) flight services, sensor integration, and aviation policy consulting. As of this enrichment pass the company publishes no public developer API, developer portal, or SDKs.

providers.name: Basalt
providers.description: Basalt (Basalt Technologies Corp.) is a San Francisco spacecraft-software company building Dispatch, a simulation-based operating system for satellites that makes flight software portable across dissimilar spacecraft hardware — pitched as "Windows for spacecraft" and "Constellations as a Service." Dispatch provides a common control layer so fleets of different satellites can work together on tasking (visible, infrared, and radar imaging), in-orbit networking and telecom, signals intelligence, and monitoring or inspecting other on-orbit assets, including autonomous re-tasking for national security missions. Founded in 2023 by Max Bhatti and Alex Choi (ex-SpaceX engineers, MIT CubeSat program), Basalt is a Y Combinator W24 company that raised a $3.5M seed round led by Initialized Capital in May 2024, with participation from Y Combinator, Liquid 2 Ventures, and General Catalyst. The company publishes no public developer API, documentation, or SDK surface; this profile captures its identity and probed domain security. Sector: frontier-tech / space / defense.

providers.name: BBN
providers.description: BBN (RTX BBN Technologies, formerly BBN Technologies and Raytheon BBN) is an American research and development organization based in Cambridge, Massachusetts, founded in 1948 and now a division of RTX Corporation. BBN has a storied history in computer networking, having built the original ARPANET Interface Message Processors and pioneered early email. Today it delivers advanced technology for national security across AI and machine learning, all-domain command and control, applied biosciences, cyber operations, spectrum dominance, maritime autonomy, multi-domain sensing, resilient networking, planning and logistics, quantum and photonics, and voice and language processing. General Catalyst has backed BBN since 2004. BBN serves government and defense customers and does not publish a public developer API, SDK, or developer portal.

providers.name: Cambridge Aerospace
providers.description: Cambridge Aerospace is a UK-based defense technology company, incorporated in September 2024, developing scalable interceptor missiles and sovereign air-and-missile-defense systems for European nations. Its first product, Skyhammer, is a tube-launched subsonic interceptor with a Cambridge-developed radar seeker, positioned as an affordable, mass-producible counter to drones and cruise missiles (often likened to an Iron Dome-style layered air defense). The company operates in the aerospace and defense/security sector and is backed by a venture syndicate including Accel, Lakestar, Lux Capital, Spark Capital, and the D3 fund. This API Evangelist profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of Accel; it is a hardware-first defense company with no public API or developer surface at this time.

providers.name: Citadel
providers.description: Citadel (also branded Citadel Defense / Drone Citadel) is a counter-unmanned-aircraft-system (C-UAS) company founded in 2016 that built an automated, modular drone-defense solution using proprietary machine-learning algorithms to detect, classify, and defeat unauthorized drones. It raised a Lightspeed Venture Partners Series A in 2017 and was subsequently acquired by BlueHalo. The company operates no public developer portal, API, SDK, or documentation surface, and its standalone domains (citadeldefense.com, dronecitadel.com) are now parked or no longer resolve.

providers.name: Distributedspectrum
providers.description: Distributed Spectrum, self-described as "The World's First AI Signals Expert," builds edge-AI radio-frequency sensing technology that detects and identifies RF signals to autonomously map threats without expensive hardware or trained operators. Its sensors process data locally to deliver real-time alerts on threat types such as tactical radios, GPS jammers, and drones, and can be deployed anywhere using commercial components to form distributed detection networks. The company is headquartered at 99 Madison Ave, New York, NY, raised a $25M Series A, and is a Felicis portfolio company. No public API or developer program is published at this time; this profile carries the identity and domain-security posture surfaced by the enrichment pipeline.

providers.name: Earendil Robotics
providers.description: Earendil Robotics is a Y Combinator-backed defense technology company registered in England and Wales that builds AI-powered situational-awareness and counter-drone systems for tactical units. Its product line includes IVAS, an edge-AI vision-augmentation system fusing night vision, thermal imaging, and laser ranging for total-darkness operation; Aeglos, an autonomous high-speed (300+ km/h) interceptor drone for counter-UAS defense with autonomous target locking and all-weather thermal tracking; and Holo, an ultra-lightweight dual-mode tactical sight combining high-resolution thermal imaging with a fiber-optic reticle. As of this profile the company exposes only a public marketing website and a contact form, with no published developer surface, API, SDKs, documentation, or GitHub organization.

providers.name: EraDrive
providers.description: EraDrive is a space technology company building compact, AI-powered self-driving modules that give spacecraft onboard autonomy — vision-based navigation, control, collision avoidance, and situational awareness computed at the edge. A Stanford Space Rendezvous Laboratory (SLAB) spinoff founded by Sumant Sharma (CEO), Justin Kruger (CTO), and Prof. Simone D'Amico (CSO), EraDrive integrates flight-proven autonomy software with existing satellite infrastructure for space traffic management, on-orbit servicing and logistics, and advanced remote sensing across commercial and defense missions. The company closed an oversubscribed $5.3M seed round in December 2025, co-led by Haystack Ventures with participation from Point Nine, Harpoon Ventures, Brave Capital, 2100 VC, and Entropy Industrial Capital. As an early-stage hardware/software company, EraDrive currently publishes no public API, developer portal, or documentation surface.

providers.name: General Radar
providers.description: General Radar Corp. (GenRad) is a Belmont, California hardtech company founded in 2016 that designs and manufactures fully solid-state, high-resolution active electronically scanned array (AESA) phased-array radar systems built largely on commercial off-the-shelf hardware. Its products include the C-band GenRad GFC multi-mission AESA radar with a GaN front-end and digital beam-forming, and the Mark-IV 76-81GHz millimeter-wave 3D imaging radar producing LIDAR-like point clouds. The company serves aerospace and defense (U.S. Air Force, Navy, NORAD), counter-drone, airfield foreign-object-debris (FOD) detection, autonomy, wind energy, and weather markets, and has raised over $35M from investors including Kleiner Perkins and Octave Ventures. General Radar publishes no public API, developer portal, SDK, or machine-readable interface; this profile is maintained for API Evangelist network completeness.

providers.name: Ghost Robotics
providers.description: Ghost Robotics designs and manufactures quadrupedal unmanned ground vehicles (Q-UGV), with its flagship Vision 60 platform deployed across defense, public safety, law enforcement, industrial, construction, and education customers. The platform supports modular payloads for sensing, comms, and manipulation. Ghost Robotics provides a developer SDK only to vetted partners and integrators and does not operate a public developer portal, open API, or public GitHub organization.

providers.name: Greypoint Industries
providers.description: Greypoint Industries is a Canadian defense-technology company (Y Combinator S26) building passive RF mapping software that charts the electromagnetic spectrum so operators can see every signal, track every threat, and act first — "built in Canada for those who protect." Founded in 2026 by Nic Chu, Jordan Khoo, Steven Xu, and Darcy Zhang, the company also develops mass-produced autonomous counter-drone interceptors designed to defeat drone-swarm saturation at a fraction of the cost of the targets. As an early-stage hardware and software startup, Greypoint currently publishes no public API, developer portal, SDK, or machine-readable specification; this profile captures the company's identity for the API Evangelist network and awaits a developer surface to enrich.

providers.name: HawkEye 360
providers.description: HawkEye 360 is a Herndon, Virginia-based radio frequency (RF) data analytics and geospatial intelligence company that operates the first commercial satellite constellation purpose-built to identify, process, and geolocate a broad range of RF signals from space. Founded in 2015 by Chris DeMay, Charles Clancy, and Bob McGwier, the company flies clusters of three small satellites in formation that use time- and frequency-difference-of-arrival triangulation to pinpoint emitters across VHF through Ku-band. As of 2025, HawkEye 360 has placed 36 Hawk satellites on orbit across 12 operational clusters. Its core products include RFGeo (the underlying RF signal mapping and geolocation data product), RFIQ (its RF intelligence data product recently selected by NASA Commercial LEO programs), and Mission Space, a web-based RF geospatial intelligence analysis platform. The company also offers a Regional Awareness Subscription (RAS) service providing persistent monitoring of high-interest regions such as the Mediterranean, South China Sea, and the Korean Peninsula. In December 2023 HawkEye 360 acquired Maxar Intelligence's RF Solutions business (formerly Aurora Insight), expanding its spectrum-mapping capabilities. Customers are concentrated in defense, intelligence, national security, and maritime domain awareness — including the US Government, allied partners, and foreign military sales (a 2025 FMS to India was approved by the Defense Security Cooperation Agency). HawkEye 360 has filed an S-1 with the SEC for a proposed IPO. There is no public, self-service developer API, SDK, or open-source release; data access is delivered through gated commercial and government contracts via the Mission Space platform and a customer-facing API for ordering and integration of RF analytics into customer systems.

providers.name: Hop Aero
providers.description: Hop Aero is a Y Combinator (Summer 2026) aerospace and defense company based in Los Angeles, California, founded in 2024 by Jacob Balaj and Matija Milenovic. The company develops hypersonic rocket cargo vehicles that deliver payloads point-to-point into austere, contested environments hundreds of miles away in minutes, aiming to give the United States and its allies an asymmetric logistics advantage. Hop Aero has raised a $3M pre-seed round and won a $1.25M U.S. Air Force SBIR award; its team draws on experience from SpaceX, Virgin Orbit, Masten Space Systems, SpinLaunch, and Destinus. This is a hardware-stage company with no public API or developer surface at the time of profiling; this record was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio-lead stub and is maintained for network discovery and enrichment.

providers.name: Hypersonica
providers.description: Hypersonica is a European defence and aerospace company developing sovereign hypersonic strike systems for both military and civilian applications. Founded to give Europe an independent technological edge to deter aggression, the company tested what it describes as Europe's first sovereign hypersonic missile prototype in February 2026, focusing on fast, modular, maneuverable deep-strike capabilities delivered in months rather than years at a claimed 80% cost reduction. Headquartered in Munich with UK offices, Hypersonica raised a EUR 23.3M Series A backed by Plural, SPRIND, and General Catalyst. As a business-to-government defence contractor it publishes no public API, developer portal, SDKs, or technical documentation, so no API artifacts could be enriched.

providers.name: Iridium
providers.description: Iridium Communications Inc. (NASDAQ: IRDM) is a McLean, Virginia satellite communications company operating a constellation of 66 cross-linked Low Earth Orbit (LEO) satellites that deliver truly global L-band voice, data, IoT, and positioning/navigation/timing (PNT) services across every region of the Earth, including the polar oceans. Iridium sells satellite phones (Iridium Extreme), satellite messengers, satellite IoT modules and modems (Iridium 9602/9603, Iridium Certus 9770/9810/9704, Iridium Edge, Iridium Edge Pro, Iridium Edge Solar), Short Burst Data (SBD) messaging, broadband Certus terminals, and next-generation Iridium NTN Direct 5G Non-Terrestrial Network services built on 3GPP NB-IoT for direct-to-device smartphone and IoT connectivity. Iridium CloudConnect — co-developed with Amazon Web Services — pipes satellite IoT data as JSON into customer-owned Amazon SQS queues inside their own AWS VPC over a dedicated private Iridium-AWS interconnect, making Iridium the first global cloud-native satellite IoT backhaul. The company serves aviation, maritime, government/defense, land-mobile, autonomous systems, and IoT markets through a partner ecosystem of more than 500 service providers, value-added resellers, and hardware OEMs, and in May 2026 announced a planned acquisition of Aireon, operator of the world's only space-based air traffic surveillance network. Iridium's business model is airtime/subscription revenue plus hardware module licensing and engineering services; there is no public, self-service developer API or OpenAPI — network access is mediated through Iridium-authorized service providers, the Iridium CloudConnect AWS integration, and hardware-level AT-command and SBD interfaces on Iridium modems.

providers.name: K2 Space
providers.description: K2 Space (K2 Space Corporation) is a Los Angeles / Torrance, California aerospace startup that designs and manufactures high-power "Mega Class" satellite buses. Its platforms deliver roughly 20kW of array power and up to one metric ton of payload capacity - about ten times the power and payload of conventional buses - to maximize the throw-weight of next-generation launch vehicles like SpaceX Starship and Blue Origin New Glenn. K2 builds radiation-tolerant, vertically integrated (80% in-house) spacecraft with redundant avionics and high-delta-v propulsion for LEO, MEO, GEO and cislunar missions, serving commercial and U.S. government / defense customers. Backed by First Round Capital, Lightspeed Venture Partners and Redpoint Ventures, the company raised a $250M Series C at a $3B valuation and is preparing its first production satellite, GRAVITAS. K2 Space is a hardware company with no public developer API; this profile tracks its identity and web presence in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Mantari
providers.description: Mantari is a weather-intelligence and earth-sensing company building a decision-intelligence platform that fuses a distributed network of sensors with AI to turn environmental data across oceans, skies, and space into mission-critical, actionable intelligence. It initially targets government and defense decision support, with plans to extend into broader economic and commercial applications. As of this profile Mantari publishes a marketing homepage and a careers page but no public API, developer portal, documentation, or SDKs; this record captures its identity plus a live domain-security probe, pending a future developer surface.

providers.name: Maquoketa Research
providers.description: Maquoketa Research is a defense-technology startup (Y Combinator, Spring 2026) building autonomous terminal-guidance systems for one-way attack drones. Its platform-agnostic guidance modules add custom computer-vision object tracking to low-cost FPV drone hardware, raising strike success rates from under 25% to roughly 80% while maintaining target lock through GPS jamming and signal loss. Founded in 2025 and based in San Francisco, the five-person team ships hardware modules (product lines include GCS, Magpie, Odin, and TGS) that integrate with existing drone flight controllers rather than a public developer API. This profile was surfaced as a Y Combinator portfolio company and enriched from the company's public website; it currently exposes no public API, SDK, or developer platform surface.

providers.name: Milliray
providers.description: Milliray is an airspace-security company building millimeter-wave radar technology to detect, track, and classify the small drones that conventional radar systems miss — from $50 quadcopters to autonomous swarms. Its DroneTector product fuses multiple sensor types into all-weather, 24/7 units that operate standalone or in networked mesh configurations, protecting airports, critical infrastructure (substations, refineries, water-treatment facilities), and forward-deployed defense operations. The company is backed by Y Combinator, NATO DIANA, the UK Defence and Security Accelerator, and the Royal Academy of Engineering. As of this enrichment pass Milliray publishes no public API, developer portal, SDK, or documentation surface — it is a hardware/defense provider without a programmable interface.

providers.name: OGSystems
providers.description: OGSystems was a geospatial intelligence, data analytics, and advanced technology company based in Chantilly, Virginia, serving the United States intelligence community and Department of Defense with threat analytics, machine learning, and geospatial exploitation solutions. The company was acquired by Parsons Corporation in 2019 and folded into Parsons' national security and intelligence portfolio. Its former domain (ogsystems.com) now redirects to parsons.com, and it maintains no independent public developer program, API reference, or machine-readable API surface. This profile is retained in the API Evangelist network as an identity/lead record surfaced from VC-portfolio data; there are no API artifacts to enrich.

providers.name: Orbital ATK
providers.description: Orbital ATK was an American aerospace manufacturer and defense industry company formed in February 2015 by the merger of Orbital Sciences Corporation and the defense and aerospace divisions of Alliant Techsystems. The company produced launch vehicles, satellites, missiles, ammunition, precision-guided munitions, rocket motors, and the Cygnus spacecraft for ISS resupply before being acquired by Northrop Grumman on June 6, 2018 and rebranded as Northrop Grumman Innovation Systems.

providers.name: Ornadyne
providers.description: Ornadyne is a Los Angeles hard-tech startup building autonomous flapping-wing UAVs (ornithopters) that look and fly like real birds for covert reconnaissance and surveillance. Its near-silent, AI-powered, man-portable drones are engineered for low acoustic and visual signatures, hour-class flight times, and natural bird-like flight, contrasting with easily detected quadcopters and fixed-wing aircraft. Founded by Geourg Kivijian (CEO, ex-NASA JPL and Astrolab) and Armen Arakelyan (CTO, ex-SpaceX Starship), the company is a Y Combinator Spring 2026 company operating in the hardware, robotics, drones, aerospace, and defense space. It is a hardware/defense company with a marketing website and no public developer API surface at this time.

providers.name: Paragon Solutions
providers.description: Paragon Solutions Ltd is an Israeli cyber-intelligence and surveillance software vendor founded in 2019 in Tel Aviv by former Unit 8200 commander Ehud Schneorson together with Idan Nurick, Igor Bogudlov and Liad Avraham, with Ehud Barak among its backers. Its flagship product, Graphite, is mobile-device intelligence software marketed to government and law-enforcement agencies. Battery Ventures took an early-stage stake in the company; in 2024 Paragon was acquired by AE Industrial Partners and merged with the US cybersecurity firm RED Lattice. Surfaced as a Battery Ventures portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network as a lead, Paragon operates no public developer platform: it publishes no API, SDKs, documentation, or self-service sign-up, and its domain (paragonsolutions.io) currently serves no website. There is no public API surface to enrich.

providers.name: Performance Drone Works
providers.description: Performance Drone Works is a company surfaced as a portfolio company of lux-capital and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. Sector: defense. This profile is a lead awaiting the enrichment pipeline.

providers.name: Philly Shipyard
providers.description: Philly Shipyard (now Hanwha Philly Shipyard, Inc.) is a commercial shipbuilder based at the former Philadelphia Naval Shipyard, constructing Jones Act-compliant container ships, product and Aframax tankers, and National Security Multi-Mission Vessels (NSMVs) for the U.S. Maritime Administration and state maritime academies. In December 2024, Hanwha Systems and Hanwha Ocean (subsidiaries of South Korea's Hanwha Group) completed the acquisition of Philly Shipyard for approximately $100M, rebranding the operation as Hanwha Philly Shipyard Inc. (HPSI). No public developer APIs have been identified at this time.

providers.name: Phoenix Tailings
providers.description: Phoenix Tailings is a clean rare earth and critical minerals refining company working to restore U.S. industrial independence by building domestic refining capacity for the metals behind every major technology. It recovers rare earth elements and other critical minerals from mining waste (tailings) and low-grade feedstocks using a low-emission, zero-landfill process, supplying materials for medical devices, electric vehicles and automotive systems, electronics, and defense applications. The company operates as a materials producer and does not currently publish a public developer API, SDK, or developer portal; this API Evangelist profile tracks its identity and web/domain security posture.

providers.name: Pratt & Whitney
providers.description: A major American aerospace manufacturer designing, manufacturing, and servicing aircraft engines for commercial, military, and business aviation applications. A division of RTX Corporation (formerly Raytheon Technologies), Pratt & Whitney is known for its geared turbofan (GTF) engine technology (PW1000G family) powering the Airbus A220 and A320neo, the F135 powering the F-35 Joint Strike Fighter, and the PT6 turboprop family. Customer-facing digital services - EngineWise health monitoring, FAST (Full-flight data Acquisition Storage and Transmission), and the Customer Portal - are operated privately for airline, MRO, and military customers behind credentialed access and are not exposed as a public developer API or open partner integration portal.

providers.name: Raphe Mphibr
providers.description: Raphe mPhibr is an Indian deep-tech aerospace company revolutionizing unmanned aviation through in-house carbon fiber composites, UAV airframes, propulsion, and end-to-end manufacturing. The company designs and builds heavy-lift and tactical unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs/drones) for defense and industrial applications, emphasizing research-driven innovation and vertically integrated production. Raphe mPhibr is a B2B / defense-oriented manufacturer surfaced as a portfolio company of General Catalyst and added to the API Evangelist network. As of this enrichment pass the company publishes no public developer portal, API, SDK, or documentation surface — its digital presence is a corporate marketing site only.

providers.name: Rise Robotics
providers.description: RISE Robotics develops industrial linear-actuation technology designed to replace traditional hydraulic systems. Its flagship Beltdraulic Cylinder is a fluid-free hydraulic alternative delivering faster actuation, higher reliability, no fire hazard, and fuel-source flexibility for large-scale industrial applications. The company builds actuation products (Beltdraulic Cylinder, Railgate, SuperJammer, CLD) for Tier 1 suppliers, OEMs, and the US Department of Defense. RISE Robotics is a hardware and heavy-equipment company backed by Techstars; it publishes no developer API, SDK, or developer portal, so this API Evangelist profile captures identity and domain-security posture only.

providers.name: Rocket Lab
providers.description: Rocket Lab (Rocket Lab Corporation, formerly Rocket Lab USA; Nasdaq RKLB) is an American aerospace manufacturer and end-to-end space company founded in 2006 by Peter Beck. It designs and launches the Electron small-lift orbital rocket, is developing the reusable Neutron medium-lift vehicle, and builds the Photon spacecraft platform along with satellites, spacecraft components, solar cells, reaction wheels, star trackers, separation systems and other space systems. Rocket Lab operates launch complexes in Mahia, New Zealand and at Wallops Island, Virginia, providing dedicated and rideshare launch services plus on-orbit management for commercial, civil and national-security customers. It was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of Khosla Ventures; this profile is enriched from public identity and live domain probes only, as Rocket Lab publishes no public developer API surface.

providers.name: Seasats
providers.description: Seasats designs and manufactures autonomous uncrewed surface vehicles (USVs) for ocean intelligence, maritime domain awareness, and defense missions. Its platform lines include the hand-deployable Lightfish (6-month endurance), the fast-response Quickfish (35+ knots with an integrated drone bay), and the heavy-payload Heavyfish. Vessels carry modular payloads, run persistent autonomous surveys, and integrate with existing command-and-control (C2) architectures. Seasats is a Techstars-backed company. As of this enrichment pass Seasats publishes no public developer API, SDK, documentation portal, or machine-readable discovery surface; its integration story is C2 interoperability, not a web API.

providers.name: SecureInfo Corporation
providers.description: SecureInfo Corporation was a cybersecurity and information-assurance company focused on FISMA and federal compliance, surfaced as a portfolio company of insight-partners and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. As of this enrichment pass the domain www.secureinfo.com no longer serves an independent site — its TLS certificate resolves to kratosdefense.com (Kratos Defense), indicating the business was acquired/absorbed. No independent public API, developer portal, or OpenAPI surface was found; this profile records that honest finding.

providers.name: Singularity
providers.description: Singularity (Singularity Defense Corp) is a defense-technology company building low-cost, mass-producible air-defense and counter-weapon systems to protect warfighters and civilians from drones and cheap aerial munitions. Founded by engineers from SpaceX, Tesla, and Anduril alongside operators who have deployed air defenses in combat, the company emerged from stealth in July 2026 with an $80M Series A at a $400M valuation led by Khosla Ventures and Felicis, with Menlo Ventures, NEA, Y Combinator, Harpoon Ventures, and others participating. It emphasizes in-house manufacturing of major subsystems combined with commercial-volume components for rapid production and field deployment, including active conflict zones. Singularity is a hardware defense company and does not publish a public API, developer portal, or SDKs. This profile was surfaced as a Menlo Ventures portfolio lead and enriched with verified company identity by the API Evangelist pipeline.

providers.name: Singularity Defense
providers.description: Singularity Defense Corp (operating on singularityus.com) is a defense-technology company building affordable, scalable counter-weapon air defense systems that protect warfighters and civilians from drones and low-cost, mass-produced munitions. Led by CEO Jack Oswald with COO Shail Giroux, the company is backed by Khosla Ventures, New Enterprise Associates, Andreessen Horowitz, Y Combinator, Menlo Ventures, and Felicis. It ships physical air-defense hardware and publishes no public API, developer portal, or developer documentation. Added to the API Evangelist network as a venture-portfolio lead; this enrichment pass confirmed the company has no public API surface.

providers.name: Surtr Defense Systems
providers.description: Surtr Defense Systems is a Y Combinator-backed defense technology company building ParallaxOS, an open operating system for counter-UAS (counter-drone) command-and-control. Surtr positions itself outside the incumbent C2 tension by not competing with hardware partners on contracts and not monetizing partner data: hardware partners decide what data the platform sees, customers decide what data is kept, and every byte is visible to partners and customers in real time. ParallaxOS ingests any sensor (radar, RF, EO/IR, acoustic) over open defense-interoperability standards such as NATO SAPIENT, Link 16, Cursor on Target, and ATAK; tasks any compatible kinetic, EW, or directed-energy effector with human-in-the-loop authorization on every engagement; and performs multi-sensor fusion, autonomous track correlation, and AI threat classification at millisecond latency on the tactical edge. Customer data, integration code, and decisions remain the customer's, deployed on-prem or in GovCloud. Founded by Anshul Ahluwalia (CEO, ex-Shield AI) and Cameron Fiore (CTO, ex-Anduril, ex-Shield AI). Added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio lead; no public developer API surface is published as of this enrichment pass.

providers.name: Target Arm
providers.description: Target Arm is a robotics company building systems to autonomously launch and recover drones from moving vehicles without stopping. Its Ralar robotic arm captures drones mid-air, recharges them, and relaunches them, while TRACKR sensor-fusion, TurboFly autopilot, and Maestro mission-control software coordinate drone fleets across commercial delivery, first-responder, agriculture, energy-inspection, and defense/ISR use cases. A Techstars-backed hardware startup with no public API or developer program at this time; this network profile captures identity and infrastructure signals only.

providers.name: Tenet Industries
providers.description: Tenet Industries is a Swedish defense-technology startup founded in 2026 by Hugo Frisk, Fabian Andersson, and Emil Falk (students from KTH Royal Institute of Technology and the Stockholm School of Economics) building low-cost, mass-producible defense systems. Applying design-for-manufacturing and first-principles engineering, the company starts with strike/attack drones — a kamikaze quadcopter that assembles in two minutes with roughly half the parts of comparable systems — and extends the same hardware/software platform to loitering munitions, jammers, radars, and missile systems. Backed by Y Combinator ($500K). As a defense hardware manufacturer, Tenet Industries currently publishes no public API, SDK, developer portal, or event surface; this profile is maintained as a company record in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Terra Industries
providers.description: Terra Industries is a Nigeria-based defense-technology company, positioning itself as Africa's first defense prime, that designs, manufactures, and deploys autonomous multi-domain security systems across air, land, and eventually sea. Founded in 2024 by Nathan Nwachuku and Maxwell Maduka, the company builds ArtemisOS (an AI-powered operating system for infrastructure security), the Archer long-range VTOL surveillance drone, the Iroko modular UAV, the Duma autonomous unmanned ground vehicle, and the Kallon solar-powered AI sentry tower to monitor, detect, and respond to threats such as terrorism, sabotage, and armed attacks on critical infrastructure including hydropower plants, mines, and power assets. Terra raised $11.75M led by 8VC in January 2026. As a hardware and defense-systems manufacturer it publishes no public API, developer portal, or technical documentation surface; this profile is maintained as a company/provider record in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Unmannd
providers.description: Unmannd (Unmannd Autonomy Pvt Ltd) is an India-based defense technology company backed by Accel and Speciale Invest, engineering autonomous drones under the banner of aerial dominance. Its TITAN 30 is an autonomous defense-logistics drone with a 30 kg max payload, 60 km/h cruise speed, 20,000 ft operational ceiling, and 30 km max range; its FURY counter-UAS interceptor was announced as launching in Q1 2026. Unmannd is a hardware/defense company and publishes no public API, developer portal, or SDKs as of July 2026.

providers.name: Ursa Space Systems
providers.description: Ursa Space Systems is an Ithaca, New York-based geospatial intelligence company that turns commercial satellite data — primarily Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) imagery, combined with electro-optical, RF, AIS, and other ground-truth feeds — into decision-ready insight reports. The company operates a GeoAI platform branded "From pixels to insights" that fuses 90+ geospatial data sources and ingests imagery from a global network of commercial SAR and EO satellite operators, then applies in-house remote-sensing, data science, and GIS expertise to deliver answers about what is happening on the ground at specific places and times. Ursa Space serves U.S. Government customers — including U.S. Space Force Space Systems Command (SSC) under INDOPACOM, AFRICOM, and SOUTHCOM, the National Geospatial-Intelligence Agency (NGA) under the Luno A and Luno B delivery orders, the Defense Innovation Unit (DIU), and humanitarian-aid agencies — as well as commercial enterprise customers in energy, commodities, supply chain, maritime, and insurance. Reporting domains span security and defense (border monitoring, military activity, maritime, dark-vessel and ship-to-ship transfer detection, airstrip monitoring), environmental and disaster response (deforestation, earthquakes, flooding, wildfires), and infrastructure and industry monitoring (construction, mining, oil and gas supply chain, power generation, space situational awareness). The platform is currently in beta and Ursa Space does not operate a public developer portal, OpenAPI reference, SDK, or self-service signup; engagement is sales-led through contact@ursaspace.com and tailored to government and enterprise contracts.

providers.name: Venus Aerospace
providers.description: Venus Aerospace is a propulsion company building the Venus Rotating Detonation Rocket Engine (RDRE) and the Venus Detonation Ramjet (VDR), a hybrid that pairs the RDRE with air-breathing ramjet technology to carry a vehicle from takeoff through hypersonic cruise on a single engine. The company positions detonation-based propulsion — supersonic detonation waves propagating around an annular combustor rather than conventional subsonic combustion — for defense munitions and uncrewed systems, space upper stages, orbital transfer vehicles and landers, and commercial high-speed flight. Venus Aerospace is a hardware and flight-test organization: it publishes a public marketing site covering the RDRE, the VDR, its team, investors and newsroom, but no developer program, API, SDK or machine-readable specification of any kind.

providers.name: VeriTX
providers.description: VeriTX Corp. is a veteran-owned blockchain and cybersecurity firm based in East Aurora, New York that builds trusted, tamper-evident data and supply-chain infrastructure originally developed for the U.S. Air Force under SBIR, STTR, and Defense Production Act programs.
