Its flagship product, QuDEFENSE, is a data-security platform that combines post-quantum cryptography with blockchain to protect sensitive files in transit and at rest, providing real-time manipulation detection, automatic quarantine of tampered data, immutable audit trails, and end-to-end data provenance. VeriTX began as a blockchain-powered digital marketplace for aerospace additive manufacturing (3D-printed aircraft parts) built on Algorand, and has since focused on secure data transfer and provenance for defense, aerospace, medical, and industrial customers. QuDEFENSE is offered as an API, an Outlook plugin, and a standalone web interface, though VeriTX does not publish a public developer portal, OpenAPI specification, or API reference documentation.

providers.name: ZeroMark
providers.description: ZeroMark is a defense-technology company building an AI-powered targeting system for counter-drone (counter-UAS) defense. Its bolt-on hardware and software components attach to existing weapons, platforms, and sensing systems to detect, track, and neutralize small drone threats in milliseconds while minimizing collateral damage. The product line spans Apex (AI aim-assist for shoulder-mounted rifles), Vanguard (a precision system for turret-mounted and vehicle platforms effective against Group 1-3 drones), and Nexus (a command-and-control software layer that integrates deployments into shared targeting and battlespace-awareness environments). ZeroMark was surfaced as a portfolio company of a16z and added to the API Evangelist network. As of this enrichment pass the company publishes no public API, SDK, developer documentation, or open-source presence; its Nexus C2 integration is delivered through defense procurement rather than a public developer program.

providers.name: Lockheed Martin
providers.description: Lockheed Martin is a leading global security, defense, and aerospace contractor. This repository captures the public APIs, developer tools, and machine-readable API artifacts where they exist for Lockheed Martin.

providers.name: GE Aerospace
providers.description: A leading manufacturer of jet engines and aviation systems for commercial and military aircraft. Spun off from General Electric to focus exclusively on aerospace propulsion and services, GE Aerospace also offers software-as-a-service tooling, engine health monitoring (Collaborative Insight), TRUEngine certification, and OnPoint maintenance and support services.

providers.name: Huntington Ingalls Industries
providers.description: Huntington Ingalls Industries is the largest military shipbuilding company in the United States, designing, building, overhauling, and repairing ships primarily for the U.S. Navy and Coast Guard, while also providing professional services including unmanned systems, defense solutions, and cybersecurity. No public developer APIs have been identified at this time.

providers.name: Allegheny Technologies
providers.description: Allegheny Technologies Incorporated (ATI) is an American producer of specialty materials headquartered in Dallas, Texas. ATI produces metals including titanium and titanium alloys, nickel-based alloys and superalloys, stainless and specialty steels, zirconium, hafnium, niobium, tungsten materials, forgings, and castings. The company serves aerospace and defense (over 50% of sales), oil and gas, chemical process industry, electrical energy, and medical markets. ATI generates approximately $4.6 billion in annual revenue and is listed on the NYSE (ticker: ATI). As a specialty materials manufacturer focused on advanced metals production, ATI does not maintain a public developer API program, but engages in EDI-based supply chain integrations with aerospace OEM customers including Boeing and Airbus.

providers.name: ATI
providers.description: ATI Inc. is a specialty materials and components manufacturer that produces high-performance alloys, titanium products, nickel-based superalloys, and engineered components. The company primarily serves the aerospace, defense, energy, electronics, and medical industries. ATI focuses on direct B2B customer relationships and does not publish a public developer API portal.

providers.name: Aliro Quantum
providers.description: Aliro Quantum (branded "Aliro, The Quantum Networking Company") is a Boston-based, Harvard spin-out building full-stack software for entanglement-based quantum networks. Its platform unifies three core products: the Aliro Simulator for physically accurate, optical-level modeling and validation of heterogeneous quantum networks before any hardware is deployed; AlirOS, a vendor-agnostic control-plane operating system that runs on quantum end-nodes and quantum repeaters across multiple hardware modalities; and the Aliro Orchestrator, a centralized single-pane-of-glass management system that configures, monitors, and operates quantum nodes and services through the full network lifecycle. These are packaged commercially as AliroNet — described by Aliro as the world's first end-to-end entanglement-based quantum network solution — delivered in three modes (Emulate, Pilot, and Deployment) and also available as AliroNet Quickstart, a bundled hardware-plus-software starter package that pairs third-party photon sources, detectors, memories, repeaters, and routers with Aliro's orchestration, control, and data operations software. The company markets Quantum-Powered Security as its anchor use case (Harvest-Now-Decrypt-Later mitigation for telcos, utilities, financial services, and defense), alongside quantum-computing interconnects (clustered and blind quantum compute for cloud providers), networked quantum sensors for positioning/navigation/timing, and quantum position verification. Customers and design partners disclosed publicly include EPB of Chattanooga, Boeing, Cisco, the US Air Force, Brookhaven National Laboratory, Stony Brook University, and Noblis. Aliro is backed by deep-tech investors including Cisco Investments and Accenture Ventures, reports more than 50 third-party quantum networking devices already integrated with its stack, and operates with hardware-agnostic positioning across photonic, trapped-ion, neutral-atom, and diamond-defect node technologies. There is no public developer API, SDK, CLI, or open-source repository — the AlirOS APIs referenced in Aliro's product materials are vendor-facing integration interfaces consumed under commercial engagement, and Aliro's GitHub organization carries no public repositories.

providers.name: Gallatin AI
providers.description: Gallatin AI builds AI-powered software for defense logistics, giving military planners and logisticians decision advantage across the tactical, operational, and strategic levels of the supply chain. Its products include Navigator, an AI decision-support "S4" that aggregates and analyzes brigade-level logistics reports in real time to streamline resupply planning; Burrow, a DoD-compliant third-party logistics (3PL) solution managing vendor qualification, transportation, inventory, storage, and fulfillment for domestic and international operations; and Phalanx, an automated asset and in-transit visibility system combining traditional reporting with hardware sensors and computer vision. Founded by veterans of Scale AI, Palantir, Amazon Prime Air, and the DoD, the company emerged from stealth in 2025 and is backed by 8VC, Silent Ventures, Timeless, Moonshots Capital, and Banter Capital.

providers.name: Raytheon
providers.description: Raytheon is an American aerospace and defense manufacturer operating as a business of RTX Corporation, the world's largest aerospace and defense company. Raytheon designs, develops, and produces advanced defense systems including precision weapons, air and missile defense systems, sensors, radar, electronic warfare, command-and-control solutions, and cyber capabilities for the U.S. military and allied governments worldwide. Key products include the Patriot missile defense system, StormBreaker smart weapons, RAIVEN electro-optical/infrared sensor suites, and advanced electronic attack systems. Raytheon also develops world-class logistics software through the EAGLE team supporting production management, technical manual development, and product support data. No public developer API or machine-readable specification is available at this time; Raytheon's software solutions are deployed within government program contracts.

providers.name: Exelis
providers.description: Exelis Inc. was an American global aerospace, defense, information, and services company that produced communications systems, electronic warfare products, geospatial systems, integrated structures, and night vision equipment. Headquartered in McLean, Virginia, Exelis was acquired by Harris Corporation in 2015. Harris and L3 Technologies then merged in 2019 to form L3Harris Technologies. No public APIs are published under the Exelis brand; developer resources, if any, are tracked under L3Harris.

providers.name: Epirus
providers.description: Epirus is a Torrance, California-based defense technology company building solid-state, software-defined high-power microwave (HPM) directed-energy systems for counter-electronics and counter-unmanned-aerial-systems (cUAS) missions. Its flagship product is Leonidas, a non-kinetic HPM weapon system designed to defeat single drones and large drone swarms by disabling their onboard electronics, with a growing product family that includes Leonidas IFPC-HPM (Indirect Fire Protection Capability — High-Power Microwave) for the U.S. Army, Leonidas Expeditionary (ExDECS) for the U.S. Marine Corps, Leonidas H2O for maritime interdiction, the portable Leonidas Pod, and Stryker Leonidas (with General Dynamics Land Systems). Epirus also collaborates with Anduril, Northrop Grumman, L3Harris, Kodiak AI, Peraton, and Palantir, and has received contracts from the U.S. Army, U.S. Air Force, U.S. Navy, DARPA, ONR, and Singapore's DSTA. The company is privately held, has raised more than $550M across Series B/C/D, and operates under CMMC Level 2 certification. Its product surface is classified defense hardware and embedded firmware — there is no public developer portal, REST API, SDK, or open-source software offering.

providers.name: L-3 Communications
providers.description: L-3 Communications was a U.S. defense prime contractor specializing in command, control, communications, intelligence, surveillance and reconnaissance (C3ISR) systems, aircraft modernization and maintenance, and government services. In 2019 L-3 merged with Harris Corporation to form L3Harris Technologies, which continues the legacy product lines and is now ranked among the top U.S. defense contractors. No public developer API has been documented.

providers.name: Northrop Grumman
providers.description: Northrop Grumman is a global aerospace, defense, and security company that delivers innovative systems, products, and solutions in autonomous systems, cyber, command and control, space, and strike weapons.

providers.name: Percipient.ai
providers.description: Percipient.ai is a Silicon Valley artificial intelligence, machine learning and computer vision company, founded in 2017 by Founder & CEO Balan Ayyar, that builds Mirage - an intelligence analysis platform for United States national security and intelligence missions. Mirage performs faster-than-real-time exploitation of unstructured multimedia, visual and multi-INT data across three modules: an FMV module for full motion video, still imagery and multi-INT sensor data supporting identity creation, network discovery, pattern-of-life analysis and geo-correlation; a cloud GSM geospatial module providing geo-fenced alerting, change detection, custom object detection and temporal analysis; and a VRM vehicle recognition module delivered as a mobile appliance for mobile and fixed surveillance with home-station cross-mission correlation. The platform is deployed both at the edge for live stream ingest and in the cloud at petabyte scale, and has been operationally procured by organizations in the US Intelligence Community and the National Geospatial-Intelligence Agency. Percipient.ai sells Mirage through federal contracting vehicles and is listed as Awardable on the CDAO Tradewinds Solutions Marketplace. It operates no public developer program: as of August 2026 it publishes no API, developer portal, API reference, SDK or machine-readable contract of any kind.

providers.name: Science Applications International Corporation (SAIC)
providers.description: Science Applications International Corporation (SAIC) is a Reston, Virginia based technology integrator that delivers mission IT, enterprise IT, engineering services, and professional services to U.S. federal civilian, defense, intelligence community, and space customers. With approximately 24,000 employees and roughly $7.3 billion in annual revenue, SAIC focuses on direct technical support and integration for government organizations, spanning CJADC2, data and AI, digital transformation, quantum technologies, cloud, cybersecurity, digital workplace, digital engineering, and systems integration. SAIC has expanded its capabilities through acquisitions including Engility (2018), Unisys Federal (2020), Halfaker (2021, DoD healthcare), Koverse (2021, secure data lake for classified environments), and Forfeiture Support Associates (2023). No public REST APIs, developer portal, OpenAPI specifications, SDKs, or open source GitHub organization have been identified for SAIC — its software and platforms are delivered under federal contract to government customers rather than as externally-consumable developer products.

providers.name: Smacktechnologies
providers.description: Smack Technologies is a frontier AI lab dedicated to national security, building domain-specific multimodal models trained via deep reinforcement learning in synthetic warfare environments to deliver decision dominance to the U.S. Department of War, its allies and partners. The company ships two product suites — Omega, a command-level AI stack pairing frontier models with customer-specific applications for strategic decision-making, and Alpha, an edge-level stack of lightweight models on proprietary hardware for tactical platforms and autonomous systems. Founded by MARSOC veterans Andrew Markoff and Clint Alanis and headquartered in El Segundo, California, Smack has raised $32M across Seed and Series A rounds led by Felicis. As of this enrichment pass the company publishes no public API, developer portal, or SDKs — a defense-domain vendor with no external developer surface.

providers.name: Vannevar Labs
providers.description: Vannevar Labs is a defense technology company building agentic AI for national security and 21st-century conflict, pre-trained for intelligence missions. Its product portfolio spans open-source intelligence and document exploitation (Decrypt, Serra, TIE, Curator), maritime domain awareness (Revere, Foreshadow), information operations (Overwatch, Local), and mission augmentation (Telescope), deployed across U.S. military bases and partner forces. Vannevar Labs operates as a sales-led, ITAR-restricted defense vendor and does not publish a public developer portal or open APIs.

providers.name: Amprius Technologies
providers.description: Amprius Technologies is a Fremont, California-based developer and manufacturer of high-energy density lithium-ion batteries built on a proprietary 100% silicon anode platform. Its flagship SiCore and SiMaxx cell families are marketed as among the industry's highest gravimetric and volumetric energy density rechargeable cells, enabling longer endurance, faster charging, and higher payload capacity than conventional graphite-anode chemistries. Amprius targets aviation and aerospace (high-altitude pseudo-satellites, unmanned aerial systems, electric vertical takeoff and landing aircraft), defense (US Army soldier-worn power, BAE Systems), light electric vehicles, robotics, and AI hardware. Public references include AALTO's Airbus-derived Zephyr HAPS programs, Prismatic's PHASA-35 stratospheric aircraft, Nokia Drone Networks, and Matternet drone delivery. The company runs pilot manufacturing and R&D in Fremont and is scaling a GWh-scale Brighton, Colorado plant alongside contract manufacturing partnerships in Asia. Amprius is publicly traded on the New York Stock Exchange under the ticker AMPX. It is certified to ISO 9001:2015 and AS9100:2016. Amprius sells cells, modules, and engineering services to OEMs and defense primes; it does not publish a developer API, SDK, or open-source battery telemetry interface, and has no public GitHub organization.

providers.name: Coreshell
providers.description: Coreshell (Coreshell Technologies, Inc.) is a San Leandro, California battery technology company founded in 2017 that develops silicon-anode lithium-ion battery cells built on low-cost, domestically sourced metallurgical-grade silicon instead of graphite or refined polysilicon. A proprietary nanolayer surface coating stabilizes the silicon anode, and the company has unveiled commercial-scale 60 Ah cells aimed at electric vehicles, defense platforms and stationary energy storage. Coreshell is a materials and cell manufacturer, not a software vendor: its public web presence is a Webflow marketing site with no developer portal, API reference, machine-readable specification, SDK, or public code repository.

providers.name: Day & Zimmermann
providers.description: Day & Zimmermann is a privately held, family-owned diversified industrial services company founded in 1901 and headquartered in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. The company operates across four primary business segments — Maintenance & Construction (power, nuclear, fossil, renewable, and chemical plants), Munitions (ammunition manufacturing, storage, and demilitarization for the U.S. military, including operation of the Lake City Army Ammunition Plant), Government Services (security, EOD, facility management, and architecture/engineering for federal agencies), and Workforce Solutions (staffing and talent placement via Yoh). The Yoh family has controlled the company since 1961; Harold L. Yoh III serves as Chairman and CEO. Day & Zimmermann reported approximately $2.7 billion in revenue in 2023 with roughly 43,000–52,000 employees across approximately 150 global locations. Day & Zimmermann does not publish any public developer APIs; its business is delivered through long-cycle service contracts, government-owned contractor-operated (GOCO) facilities, and direct client engagements.

providers.name: Plexus
providers.description: Plexus is a global manufacturing and product development company that helps customers in highly regulated industries (Aerospace/Defense, Healthcare/Life Sciences, Industrial, and Semiconductor Capital Equipment) design, manufacture, and service their products. Plexus does not currently publish a public developer API; this index tracks customer/supplier portals and corporate web properties.

providers.name: ManTech International
providers.description: ManTech International is a Herndon, Virginia-based federal services contractor providing cybersecurity, data and AI, digital transformation, and intelligent engineering capabilities to U.S. defense, intelligence, and federal civilian agencies. Founded in 1968 and publicly traded on NASDAQ as MANT until 2022, the company was acquired by The Carlyle Group in April 2022 in an all-cash take-private transaction valued at approximately $4.2 billion and now operates as a Carlyle portfolio company. ManTech holds positions on major federal contract vehicles including Alliant 2/3, OASIS+, SeaPort NxG, CIO-SP3, T4NG, and ICON, and does not publish any developer-facing API or public OpenAPI surface.

providers.name: Nlight
providers.description: nLIGHT, Inc. (NASDAQ: LASR) is a US-based designer and manufacturer of high-power semiconductor and fiber lasers, optical fibers, and beam-control systems. For more than 25 years the company has served mission-critical directed-energy and defense, sensing, and advanced-manufacturing markets (cutting, welding, additive, medical, and battery production) from a vertically integrated stack spanning semiconductor chips to complete laser systems, with a portfolio of over 450 patents and design and manufacturing based in Camas, Washington. nLIGHT is a hardware and photonics company and publishes no public developer API, SDK, or developer portal.

providers.name: Reach Labs
providers.description: Reach Labs (operating as Reach Power Inc.) is a wireless power transmission company that delivers electrical energy through the air without physical connections, describing its mission as "doing for power what Wi-Fi did for data." Its patented approach combines energy-transmission hardware, a custom delivery algorithm, and adaptive software controls to beam power to devices across varying distances and conditions. The company targets three primary sectors: defense and intelligence (powering sensors, autonomous vehicles, and drones in remote environments), manufacturing and logistics (energizing robotics and IoT devices in industrial settings), and public safety (enabling continuous drone operations for first responders). Reach was surfaced as a portfolio company of DCVC and added to the API Evangelist network. As of this enrichment pass the company publishes no public API, SDK, developer portal, or machine-readable metadata surface.

providers.name: BBN Technologies
providers.description: BBN Technologies is a research and development organization founded in 1948 (originally Bolt Beranek and Newman) and now operating as RTX BBN Technologies, a division of RTX (Raytheon). BBN is historically notable for pioneering the ARPANET, early network email, and packet-switched networking, and today conducts advanced defense and intelligence R&D across AI/machine learning, command and control, cyber operations, signal processing and spectrum, networking, quantum and photonics, and voice and language technologies. BBN serves government and defense customers and does not publish a public developer portal, API, or SDK surface; this profile is maintained for network identity and discovery only.

providers.name: Defense Counterintelligence and Security Agency
providers.description: The Defense Counterintelligence and Security Agency (DCSA) is the largest security agency in the federal government, dedicated to protecting America's trusted workforce and trusted workspaces. DCSA conducts personnel vetting and background investigations, oversees the National Industrial Security Program, delivers counterintelligence and insider threat support, and operates systems such as the Defense Information System for Security (DISS) and the National Background Investigation Services (NBIS). DCSA does not currently expose a public developer API; access to its mission systems is limited to authorized government users and cleared industry partners.

providers.name: KBR
providers.description: KBR is a Fortune 500 company that delivers science, technology, and engineering solutions to governments and companies around the world, spanning defense, intelligence, space, energy transition, and sustainable infrastructure markets.

providers.name: Benchmark Electronics
providers.description: Benchmark Electronics, Inc. is an advanced electronics engineering and manufacturing services (EMS) company headquartered in Tempe, Arizona. The company provides integrated design, engineering, and manufacturing services from prototypes to high-volume production, including procurement, logistics, and repair. Benchmark serves original equipment manufacturers in defense, medical technologies, commercial aerospace, industrial, next-gen communications, advanced computing, and semiconductor capital equipment markets. The company operates approximately 22 locations in 8 countries with around 13,000 employees.

providers.name: Chariot Defense
providers.description: Chariot Defense is a San Francisco-area defense technology company building high-voltage, hybrid-electric power systems for the modern battlefield. Its AMPHORA family (the 24 VDC / 5 kW A24 and the 400 VDC / 35 kW A400) and the upcoming VANGUARD platform deliver quiet, high-density, transportable power that replaces loud, fuel-hungry diesel generators, cutting energy signature and fuel use while powering distributed systems such as drones, sensors, electronic warfare, command and control, additive manufacturing, and directed-energy weapons. Founded in 2022 by Adam Warmoth, the company has raised $41M (a $34M Series A led by Andreessen Horowitz plus an $8M seed) and its systems are fielded by the U.S. Army and the Defense Innovation Unit. This is a hardware/defense company profiled in the API Evangelist network; it publishes no public developer API, portal, or documentation.

providers.name: Curtiss-Wright
providers.description: Curtiss-Wright is a global integrated business that provides highly engineered products, solutions, and services mainly to the aerospace, defense, commercial power, process, and general industrial markets. Its product portfolio spans rugged embedded computing, mission-critical avionics, electronic packaging, naval propulsion, reactor coolant pumps for nuclear power, surface treatment services, industrial valves, sensors, data acquisition systems, telemetry ground stations, emergency arresting systems for military aircraft, and electronic systems for naval shipbuilding programs. The company traces its lineage to the aviation pioneers Glenn Curtiss and the Wright brothers and today operates across the Defense Electronics, Naval & Power, and Aerospace & Industrial segments.

providers.name: Icarus
providers.description: Icarus is an aerospace and defense company building autonomous, solar-powered stratospheric aircraft for persistent surveillance and connectivity. Its APOLLO platform operates continuously above 60,000 feet, delivering rapid aerial intelligence, wide-area coverage across 1,000+ square miles, and always-on, low-latency (5-10ms) direct-to-device communications for weeks-long missions without ground infrastructure. Founded in 2023 and based in El Segundo, California, Icarus was part of Y Combinator's Fall 2025 batch. The company operates in the defense/aerospace hardware space and does not currently publish any public API, developer portal, SDK, or technical developer surface; this profile captures its identity for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Linear Labs
providers.description: Linear Labs is an industrial motor technology company headquartered in Fort Worth, Texas, building high-torque motor systems for wind, nuclear, pumps, actuators, mining, and defense applications. Its patented Hunstable Electric Turbine (HET) permanent-magnet architecture uses a circumferential flux design the company states delivers 2x torque density, 97% peak efficiency, and 50% weight reduction versus conventional motors, scaling from 10 kW to 2.2 MW. Its PitchPro 2000 is a complete pitch-system replacement for aging GE 1.5 wind turbines, pairing the HET motor with KEBA drive electronics, a Bachmann PLC controller, and ultracapacitor backup power. Linear Labs is a hardware manufacturer and publishes no public API, developer portal, or machine-readable technical surface; this profile is maintained for network coverage and identity only.

providers.name: Marianaminerals
providers.description: Mariana Minerals is a software-first, vertically integrated critical-minerals company supplying the metals essential to modern energy, artificial intelligence, and defense technologies. The company currently develops copper and lithium production projects, with plans spanning cobalt, aluminum, graphite, uranium, and rare earth metals, and is headquartered in San Francisco with an engineering office in Houston. Backed by Khosla Ventures, it was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio lead; an enrichment pass found no public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface.

providers.name: NPco
providers.description: NPco (NP Company) is an AI-native physics-simulation startup building AI-powered simulation for aerospace, defense, and energy engineering. Backed by Partech, it positions itself around accelerating physics simulation with AI. As of this enrichment pass the company publishes only a marketing site (careers plus a contact@npco.ai address) with no public developer portal, API, documentation, or SDKs surfaced. This profile remains a lead in the Industrial, Energy & IoT sector pending any future developer/API surface.

providers.name: Zeno Power Systems
providers.description: Zeno Power Systems (Zeno Power) develops radioisotope power systems — compact "nuclear batteries" that convert the decay heat of radioisotopes into long-duration electricity for extreme environments such as the lunar surface, deep-sea infrastructure, and remote defense installations. Backed by Techstars and other investors, Zeno is a hardware and energy-systems company; as of this enrichment pass it publishes no public web API, developer portal, documentation, SDK, or GitHub organization, so this profile is identity-only.

providers.name: V2X
providers.description: V2X is a defense and national security contractor providing mission-critical solutions including AI integration, cybersecurity, advanced engineering, operations support, training, and modernization services. The company serves U.S. government, allied defense, and aerospace customers globally. V2X does not publish a public developer API portal.

providers.description: Profile for Viasat in the API Evangelist network. Fortune F1000 (rank 972).

providers.name: Navy
providers.description: The U.S. Navy plays a crucial role in defending national security and protecting the country's interests at sea. It operates a fleet of ships and submarines, as well as aircraft and personnel, to conduct a range of missions, including maritime patrol, reconnaissance, and combat operations. The Navy also performs humanitarian missions, such as disaster relief and search and rescue efforts. No public APIs have been identified at this time. The previously listed CNATRA "API" reference is an Aviation Preflight Indoctrination training video library, not a programmatic API.

providers.name: Zeno Power
providers.description: Zeno Power is a deep-tech energy company developing radioisotope power systems (nuclear batteries) that convert the heat of radioisotope decay into reliable, long-duration electricity for extreme environments where conventional power sources fail. Its compact radioisotope Stirling generators target 1-100+ watts for use cases spanning NASA lunar surface missions (americium-241 fueled), seabed and maritime sensor infrastructure, and Department of Defense / U.S. Space Force applications (strontium-90 fueled). The company works with partners including NASA, the Pentagon, Westinghouse, and Orano, with commercial market delivery targeted for 2027. Backed by DCVC, Zeno Power was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio lead; enrichment found no public API, developer platform, SDKs, or technical documentation surface as of this pass.

providers.name: PAE
providers.description: PAE (Pacific Architects and Engineers) was a U.S. federal services contractor providing mission support, training, intelligence, and infrastructure services to U.S. government agencies and allied governments. Founded in 1955, PAE was publicly traded on NASDAQ under ticker symbol "PAE" until its acquisition by Amentum on February 15, 2022, in an all-cash transaction valued at approximately $1.9 billion (including assumed debt). PAE was fully absorbed into Amentum and no longer operates as a standalone brand. The pae.com domain now redirects to Amentum properties. PAE never published a public developer program, API portal, OpenAPI specifications, SDKs, or any public-facing technical APIs — its business was federal services delivery, not software or platforms. This profile is maintained for historical completeness within the API Evangelist network registry.

providers.name: Delta Tucker Holdings
providers.description: Delta Tucker Holdings was the holding company for DynCorp International, a provider of specialized mission-critical professional and support services to government and commercial customers, including aviation services, logistics, and training. DynCorp's operations were acquired and integrated into Amentum in 2020. Delta Tucker Holdings does not publish public APIs; this profile is preserved as a corporate-history index.

providers.name: Kumu Networks
providers.description: Kumu Networks, Inc. is a Sunnyvale, California semiconductor and RF technology company founded in 2011 to commercialize Stanford University research into full-duplex wireless and self-interference cancellation (SIC). Its silicon and module products — RF integrated circuits, cancellers such as the K8 canceller prototype, and self-interference-cancelling smart repeaters — let a radio transmit and receive on the same or an adjacent channel at the same time, across roughly 200 MHz to 60 GHz, targeting 4G/5G/6G infrastructure, Wi-Fi, IoT, satellite, and defense and aerospace programs including US Army demonstrations and Department of Defense dynamic spectrum-sharing work. The company raised roughly $45M from investors including Khosla Ventures, New Enterprise Associates, Cisco Investments, Deutsche Telekom, Verizon Ventures, Swisscom, Singtel Innov8 and Third Point, and its shares trade on secondary marketplaces. Kumu Networks licenses hardware IP and sells modules to wireless equipment manufacturers rather than operating a public developer platform: as of August 2026 it publishes no developer portal, API documentation, OpenAPI/AsyncAPI specification, SDKs, CLI or public code repositories, and its own website at kumunetworks.com returns HTTP 404 from its WP Engine host (last successful Internet Archive capture 2024-08-10).

providers.name: 8VC
providers.description: 8VC is a technology investment firm founded in 2015 by Joe Lonsdale and Jake Medwell (with founding partners Drew Oetting and Kimmy Scotti) following the wind-down of Formation 8, and headquartered at 907 South Congress Avenue in Austin, Texas after relocating from San Francisco in 2020. The firm both invests in and co-founds early-stage companies, dedicating a significant share of its capital (roughly 25-30%) to building companies from scratch through its "8VC Build" venture-studio program and assembling teams of top specialists. 8VC concentrates on "national capability" and deep-tech categories including defense, life sciences and biotech, healthcare, logistics and supply chain, manufacturing and industrials, enterprise software, financial services, AI, and IT infrastructure. With approximately $6 billion in assets under management (2023) and a public portfolio of more than 170 companies, 8VC is known for its founder-led, mission-driven approach and notable investments including Palantir, Addepar, Anduril, Flexport, Vercel, Saronic, Epirus, Yugabyte, and Project44. The firm runs the 8VC Fellowship and Bio-IT Fellowship talent programs and maintains a stated policy of not accepting capital from foreign-government-connected sources.

providers.name: General Catalyst
providers.description: General Catalyst is a global venture capital and investment firm founded in 2000 by Joel Cutler and David Fialkow, headquartered in Cambridge, Massachusetts, with offices in San Francisco, New York, London, Berlin, Bengaluru, and Washington, D.C. The firm invests across seed, venture, and growth stages and manages more than $43 billion in assets under management (as of December 2024), backing 900+ portfolio companies. General Catalyst operates through distinct capital vehicles and initiatives — Ignition/Seed for early-stage, Endurance/Grow for growth, Creation for company building, and a dedicated Health Assurance practice for healthcare transformation. Its current "Global Resilience" thesis, led by CEO Hemant Taneja, concentrates on the critical systems that underpin modern society — healthcare, energy, defense, and AI — alongside an "unscaling" thesis that uses data and AI to personalize core societal services. Notable investments include Airbnb, Stripe, Anthropic, Canva, HubSpot, Ramp, Anduril, Applied Intuition, Samsara, Mistral, Helsing, Hippocratic AI, and Mercor.

providers.name: Lux Capital
providers.description: Lux Capital is a New York City-based venture capital firm founded in 2000 by Josh Wolfe, Peter Hebert, and Robert Paull that backs entrepreneurs building companies at the frontier of science and technology, turning "sci-fi into sci-fact." The firm systematically mines academia and government research labs for breakthrough technologies that have matured beyond proof-of-concept but have not yet attracted mainstream venture attention, then makes long-term bets on contrarians and outsiders challenging the status quo. Lux invests primarily at early stage across three focus areas: AI and technology, defense/space/ manufacturing, and biotech/healthcare, with an emphasis on deep tech, robotics, and emerging science. The firm manages roughly $7 billion in assets under management across nine core funds, closing Lux Ventures IX at $1.5 billion in January 2026, and has invested in over 200 companies. Through Lux Labs, launched in 2024, the firm has also helped create more than 20 new companies. Notable portfolio companies include Anduril, Applied Intuition, Databricks, Cognition, Ramp, Runway, Recursion Pharmaceuticals, Planet, and Saildrone. Lux is headquartered in New York City with an additional office in Silicon Valley.
